position: The one of pure knowledge is God, and scriptural knowledge bears fruit by worship that cuts off rebirth.
quote: ஆகம அறிவிற்குப் பயன் அவன் தாளைத் தொழுது பிறவியறுத்தல்

position: The one meant is any person greater in knowledge, and the failing is a lack of humility before such people.
quote: தன்னைவிட அறிவில் மூத்த பெருந்தகையாளரின் முன்னே வணங்கிநிற்கும் பண்பு

position: The long life is deathless life in the world of release, above all worlds.
quote: எல்லா உலகிற்கும் மேலாய் வீட்டு உலகின்கண் அழிவின்றி வாழ்வார்

position: The general word 'land' covers this world and the next, with enjoyment named before release.
quote: இவ்வுலகின்கண்ணும் மேலுலகின்கண்ணு மென்று கொள்ளப்படும்

position: The long life is the lasting renown of those who follow such a person.
quote: புகழ்வாழ்வு, உலகில் நெடுங்காலம் நிலைத்து நிற்கும்.

position: The suffering removed is that of rebirth, in its three classical kinds.
quote: எக்காலத்தும் பிறவித் துன்பங்கள் உளவாகா.

position: The one meant is a selfless human example, and following such a person keeps ordinary suffering away.
quote: விருப்பு வெறுப்பற்றுத் தன்னலமின்றித் திகழ்கின்றவரைப் பின்பற்றி நடப்பவர்களுக்கு

position: Even good deeds cause birth, and the praise is true only of the one who has all divine qualities.
quote: நல்வினையும் பிறத்தற்கு ஏதுவாகலான்

position: Those who understand what 'the Lord' means and seek renown meet good and bad with equal measure.
quote: நன்மை தீமைகளை ஒரே அளவில் எதிர் கொள்வார்கள்.

position: The other seas are wealth and pleasure, set apart from virtue in the three aims of life.
quote: ஏனைப் பொருளும் இன்பமும் 'பிற' எனப்பட்டன.

position: The அந்தணன் is a worthy human being, whose example carries others across seas of trouble.
quote: அந்தணர் என்பதற்குப் பொருள் சான்றோர் என்பதால்,

position: The eight qualities are those taught in the Saiva agamas, though others list them differently.
quote: இவ்வாறு சைவாகமத்துக் கூறப்பட்டது.

position: The sea is the shoreless chain of cause and effect in rebirth.
quote: காரண காரியத் தொடர்ச்சியாய் கரை இன்றி வருதலின்

position: The sea is life in this world, which is hard to cross without following a leading person.
quote: வாழ்க்கை எனும் பெருங்கடலை நீந்திக் கடக்க

note: The opening verse sets the world under a First One without reservation. In 1062, Valluvar curses whoever ordered the world so that people must beg to live. Read together, they show the book does not treat the world's source as beyond moral judgement.
Here learning has no fruit without bowing at the feet. In 400, learning itself is the one imperishable wealth, with no such condition.
The same word, ஐந்தவித்தான், describes the Lord here and a human renunciant in 25. Sharing the epithet suggests that the divine model and the human achievement are not wholly separate.
Here only those at the Lord's feet cross the sea of births. In 38, on the commentators' reading, a daily good deed blocks the road of births, and God is not mentioned.

position: தடிந்து means the cloud scoops up the sea's water, and the sea's 'nature' is its living creatures and gems.
quote: ஈண்டுக் 'குறைத்தல்' என்றது முகத்தலை.

position: He takes the word as the cloud flashing, and reports that others read it as dividing.
quote: மின்னி மழையானது பெய்யாவிடின்

position: The verse also teaches that those who rise from a society must serve it for it to live.
quote: மனித சமுதாயத்திலிருந்து புகழுடன் உயர்ந்தவர்களும் அந்தச் சமுதாயத்திற்கே பயன்பட்டால்தான் அந்தச் சமுதாயம் வாழும்.

position: ஒழுக்கு is the unceasing flow of water, and he records the conduct reading as someone else's.
quote: அந்நீர் இடையறாது ஒழுகும் ஒழுக்கும் வானை இன்றி அமையாது.

position: ஒழுக்கு is conduct, which may decay if there is no rain.
quote: உலகில் மழையே இல்லையென்றால் ஒழுக்கமே கெடக்கூடும்

note: In 1031, the whole world follows the plough. This verse adds what the praise of agriculture leaves out: the plough itself follows the rain.
Here giving and austerity cannot last without rain. In 34, virtue is simply a spotless mind and everything else is noise. If virtue is only inward, the drought in 19 shouldn't threaten it.
Hunger is here the world's worst consequence of drought, a natural evil. In 225, relieving hunger outranks the ascetic's power to endure it, which turns this natural fact into a moral priority.

position: This is a shared conclusion of all religious texts, though they conflict on everything else.
quote: ஒன்றையொன்று ஒவ்வாத சமய நூல்கள் எல்லாவற்றிற்கும் இஃது ஒத்த துணிவு

position: Even a false text praises renunciants, so that people will honour it.
quote: யாதானுமொரு பொய்யைச் சொல்லும் நூலும்

position: The two are birth and release, weighed for their suffering and joy, and the virtue taken up is renunciation.
quote: பிறப்பு வீடு என்னும் இரண்டனது துன்ப இன்பக் கூறுபாடுகளை ஆராய்ந்து அறிந்து

position: The two are good and evil, and anyone who chooses the good is great.
quote: நன்மை எது, தீமை எது என்பதை ஆய்ந்தறிந்து

position: Indra, cursed for failing to quench the five, shows by his own failure what the power is worth.
quote: தான் ஐந்து அவியாது சாபம் எய்தி நின்று, அவித்தவனது ஆற்றல் உணர்த்தினான்

position: Indra trembles for his throne when anyone does great penance, so the ascetic is stronger than the gods.
quote: அவன் தன் பதம் இழக்கின்றானாக நடுங்குமாதலான்

position: What is hard is the eight limbs of yoga; what is easy is following the senses.
quote: செயற்கு அரிய ஆவன, இமயம், நியமம் முதலாய எண்வகை யோக உறுப்புக்கள்.

position: Those who have renounced are still small if they can't do these hard things.
quote: துறந்த மாத்திரத்தானே பெரியரென்று கொள் ளப்படார்

position: This is knowledge of the twenty-five principles of Samkhya, beyond which there is no world.
quote: சாங்கிய நூலுள் ஓதியவாற்றான் ஆராய்தல்.

position: This is the ability to understand and master the senses, which the world honours.
quote: ஐம்புலன்களின் இயல்பை உணர்ந்து அவற்றை அடக்கியாளும் திறன் கொண்டவனையே உலகம் போற்றும்.

position: Renunciants' words take effect, and their commanding mantras prove it visibly.
quote: அவர் ஆணையாகச் சொல்லிய மந்திரங்களே கண்கூடாகக் காட்டும்.

position: 'Full' describes people of complete learning, whose mantras circulate as proof.
quote: நிரம்பிய கல்வியையுடைய மாந்தரது

position: The proof is the enduring ethical books of the worthy.
quote: அவர்களது அறவழி நூல்களே எடுத்துக் காட்டும்.

position: Their anger lasts only a moment, yet its target cannot ward it off.
quote: தான் உள்ள அளவு கணமே ஆயினும், வெகுளப்பட்டாரால் தடுத்தல் அரிது.

position: The harm from their anger can't be avoided, as in Nahusha's becoming a serpent.
quote: நகுஷன் பெரும்பாம்பாயினான்.

position: Such people can't hold on to anger, even for a moment.
quote: அந்தக் கோபம் அவர்கள் உள்ளத்தில் ஒரு கணம்கூட நிலைத்து நிற்காது.

position: The name's reason restricts it to those with such grace, namely those in renunciation.
quote: அந்தணரென்று சொல்லப்படுவார் துறவறத்தில் நின்றவர்.

position: Having said some renunciants are small, the verse says some non-renunciants are great.
quote: துற வாதாரினும் பெரியாருளரென்று கூறினார்.

position: Any worthy person with love for all beings is an அந்தணர்.
quote: சான்றோர் எவராயினும் அவர் அந்தணர் எனப்படுவார்.

note: Here the texts' settled view exalts renouncers above all. In 49, on Parimelazhagar's reading, the thing called virtue is household life, and renunciation is good only if it is blameless. The book states both verdicts without reconciling them.
Both define greatness by rare, difficult acts. Chapter 3 says this of renouncers, while 975 in the chapter on greatness says it of the great in general, so the test is not limited to ascetics.

Here the sage's unstoppable anger shows his stature. In 301, real restraint means holding anger back exactly where it can hurt. By the standard of 301, the anger praised in 29 is what should be held back.
Both make conduct the test of priestly status: 30 defines அந்தணர் by compassion, and 134 says a பார்ப்பான் is lost if conduct fails, even though forgotten scripture can be relearned.

position: When the body dies, virtue stays joined to the soul and travels into the next body.
quote: செய்த உடம்பு அழியவும் உயிரோடு ஒன்றி ஏனை உடம்பினுட் சேறலின்

position: Virtue survives as lasting renown after death.
quote: அது ஒருவர் இறந்தபின் கூட அழியாப் புகழாய் நிலைத்துத் துணை நிற்கும்.

position: Rider and bearer are direct perceptual evidence of virtue's fruit, so scripture needn't be cited.
quote: சிவிகையைக் காவுவானோடு செலுத்துவானிடைக் காட்சியளவை தன்னானே உணரப்படும்.

position: This is an analogy of attitude: the virtuous ride through joy and sorrow lightly, and others carry life as a burden.
quote: வாழ்க்கையில் வரும் இன்ப துன்பங்கள் இரண்டையும் எளியவாகக் கருதி மகிழ்வுடன் பயணத்தை மேற்கொள்வார்கள்.

position: The stone blocks the road by which embodied days would return, which means it ends rebirth.
quote: அச்செயல் அவன் யாக்கையோடு கூடும் நாள் வரும் வழியை வாராமல் அடைக்குங் கல்லாம்.

position: The stone is a paving stone that smooths the road of this life.
quote: வாழ்க்கைப் பாதையைச் சீராக்கி அமைத்துத் தரும் கல்லாக

position: The joy is sensual enjoyment that accords with household life; illicit pleasure turns to pain.
quote: இல்லறத்தோடு பொருந்தி வருவதே இன்பம் ஆவது

position: All enjoyment of any kind comes through virtue.
quote: இஃது எல்லாப் போக நுகர்ச்சியும் இதனானே வருமென்றது.

position: The joy arises from the renown a virtuous life brings.
quote: அறவழி வாழ்க்கையில் வருகின்ற புகழால் ஏற்படுவதே இன்பமாகும்.

note: Here outward virtue is noise if the mind is stained. In 280, a shaven head and matted hair are unnecessary if one avoids what the world condemns. Note that 280 keeps the world's blame as the test, so the inward standard of 34 isn't all that matters.
Both press virtue into the present against the delay of 'later'. 36 promises a companion, and 335 frightens with the hiccup that stops the tongue. Each uses a different motive for the same urgency.

On the commentators' reading, 37 treats the difference between rider and bearer as virtue made visible. In 972, birth is the same for all beings, and distinction comes from what one does, which still leaves open whether the palanquin bearer's lot is deserved.

position: The three are the other life-stages, and he says Valluvar takes the first two from other people's doctrine.
quote: இவருள் முன்னை இருவரையும் பிறர் மதம் மேற்கொண்டு கூறினார்.

position: The three are one's parents, spouse and children.
quote: பெற்றோர், வாழ்க்கைத் துணை, குழந்தைகள் என இயற்கையாக அமைந்திடும் மூவர்க்கும்

position: துறந்தார் are people abandoned by those who should support them, and இறந்தார் are those who die alone at the door.
quote: களைகண் ஆனவரால் துறக்கப்பட்டார்க்கும்

position: துறந்தார் are renouncers who have given up caste and name.
quote: வருணத்தினையும் நாமத்தினையுந் துறந்தார்க்கும்

position: They are ascetics, the hungry and the unprotected, so there is no duty to the dead here.
quote: பற்றற்ற துறவிகட்கும், பசியால் வாடுவோர்க்கும், பாதுகாப்பற்றவர்க்கும்

position: If someone shares wealth that was wrongly taken, the merit goes to the owner and the sin stays with the sharer.
quote: அறம் பொருளுடையார் மேலும், பாவம் தன் மேலுமாய் நின்று வழி எஞ்சும்

position: The outside way is only the forest stage, which leaves full renunciation out of the comparison.
quote: இல்லை விட்டு வனத்துச் செல்லும் நிலை.

position: The outside way is austerity in general, and the householder gets the fruit of austerity too.
quote: புறநெறியாகிய தவத்திற் போய்ப் பெறுவது யாதோ?

position: Those striving are ascetics trying to give up the senses, and the householder gets the result without such effort.
quote: புலன்களை விட முயல்வார் எல்லாருள்ளும் மிக்கவன்.

position: Those striving are people striving for wealth.
quote: முயறல் - பொருட்கு முயறல்.

position: The householder also endures the troubles that come upon others.
quote: பிறரை உற்ற நோயும் பொறுத்தல் இன்மையின்

position: 'That too' is renunciation, which is good only if it is free of hypocrisy.
quote: ஏனைத் துறவறமோ எனின், அதுவும் பிறனால் பழிக்கப்படுவது இல்லையாயின்

position: 'That too' is household life, and the blame in question would be a wife of low birth.
quote: பழிக்கப்படுவதென்றது இழிகுலத்தாளாகிய மனையாளை.

position: A blameless household life is what is honoured as the household dharma.
quote: பழிப்புக்கு இடமில்லாத இல்வாழ்க்கை இல்லறம் எனப் போற்றப்படும்.

note: In 23 those who weigh both paths and take up virtue here stand highest in the world. In 46 the householder has nothing to gain by leaving. Parimelazhagar resolves this by limiting 46 to the forest stage, but the verse doesn't state that limit.
Sharing food is a household duty here, and in 322 it becomes the chief of all that the authors have listed. What began as one household rule becomes the book's summary of virtue.

Here a well-lived earthly life earns a place among the gods. In 234 earthly renown goes further, so that the gods' world ceases to praise its own sages. Both measure human achievement against heaven and rate it highly.

position: A wife is ranked among the things a man can obtain, and none is better.
quote: ஒருவன் எய்தும் பொருள்களுள் இல்லாளின் மேம்பட்ட பொருள்கள் யாவை உள

position: The comparison is about being born a woman, which nothing exceeds if it has this firmness.
quote: பெண் பிறப்புப்போல் மேம்பட்டன யாவையுள்?

position: The firmness is womanhood's own strength of character.
quote: பெண்மையின் உறுதிப் பண்பைப் பெற்றுவிட்டால்,

position: Her husband is her own god, and her steadfastness is so powerful that the deities obey her.
quote: பிற தெய்வம் தொழாது தன் தெய்வம் ஆகிய கொழுநனைத் தொழாநின்று துயிலெழுவாள்

position: She regards all gods as being her husband.
quote: எல்லாத் தெய்வ முந் தன்கணவனென்றே கருதி

position: Such a wife is like rain falling in fear at a command: she has made herself a slave.
quote: அஞ்சி நடுங்கிப் பெய்கின்ற மழையைப் போலத் தன்னை அடிமையாக எண்ணிக் கொள்பவளாவாள்.

position: Walls and door-guards are useless without நிறை, the holding of her heart to chastity.
quote: காவல் இரண்டினும் நிறைக் காவல் இல்வழி ஏனைச் சிறைக்காவலால் பயன் இல்லை

position: The verse is a charge against men: treating such women as slaves is ignorance.
quote: அடிமைகளாக நடத்த எண்ணுவது அறியாமையாகும்.

position: The missing word is worship: women who serve their husbands are honoured by the gods.
quote: தற்கொண்டாற் பேணிய மகளிர் புத்தேளிரால் பேணப்படுவர்

position: If a woman obtains a virtuous husband, household life becomes a new world for her.
quote: நற்பண்பு பெற்றவனைக் கணவனாகப் பெற்றால்,

note: Verse 9 calls a head that does not bow to the Lord's feet useless. Here a woman who does not worship a god is the one whom the rain obeys. Parimelazhagar's added 'other gods' softens the contrast, but the Tamil does not contain it.
In 18, even the gods' worship depends on rain. Here rain answers to a woman who bypasses the gods. Together the two verses invert the expected order of gods, rain and humans.

The wife lives within her husband's income, and 478 applies the same rule to the king's treasury: a small inflow is no ruin if outflow doesn't widen. The Kural's household economics and statecraft share one rule.

Here நிறை is the guard that outdoes all confinement. In 1251, speaking as a woman in love, desire's axe breaks the door of நிறை barred with shame. The book's ethics section treats inner guard as sufficient, and its love section knows it isn't.

position: The epithet of understanding restricts மக்கள் to sons, excluding daughters.
quote: 'மக்கள்' என்னும் பெயர் பெண் ஒழித்து நின்றது.

position: The verse is about intelligent children in general, with no such exclusion.
quote: அறிவில் சிறந்த நல்ல பிள்ளைகளைவிட

position: Sons' good deeds done on the parents' behalf bring what they earned to the parents in the next world.
quote: அப்புதல்வர் செய்த பொருள் தம்மை நோக்கி அவர் செய்யும் நல்வினையானே தம்பால் வரும்

position: Each child's wealth comes from that child's own actions.
quote: அம்மக்களின் பொருள்கள் அவரவர் செயல்களின் விளைவாக வரக் கூடியவை.

position: It is sweeter to all the world, especially the assembly, than it is to the parents.
quote: மன்உயிர்க்கு எல்லாம் தம்மின் இனிது

position: It concerns children who are wiser than their parents, which gladdens everyone.
quote: பெற்றோரைக் காட்டிலும் பிள்ளைகள் அறிவிற் சிறந்து விளங்கினால்,

position: She has to hear it because, by a woman's nature, she cannot judge it herself.
quote: பெண்ணியல்பால் தானாக அறியாமையின் 'கேட்ட தாய்'

note: Rain is the world's amrita in 11, and in 64 a child's messy gruel beats amrita. The same word is the top of two different scales: what sustains all life, and what is sweet to one parent.

Parimelazhagar's two comments pull apart. On 63 a son's good deeds reach his parents. On 377 he says the fruit of one soul's deed never goes to another (ch038). The verses themselves don't settle how merit is shared.

The father's debt and the son's debt form an exchange: he gives the learning that seats the son at the front, and the son gives back a sentence of praise. Parimelazhagar's gloss on 70 makes the link explicit by calling the father 'the one who made him learned'.

position: The soul is joined to a body for the purpose of love, since love can't be done without one.
quote: உடம்போடு இயைந்தல்லது அன்பு செய்யலாகாமையின், அது செய்தற் பொருட்டு இத்தொடர்ச்சி உளதாயிற்று

position: The present embodiment results from love practised in a previous birth.
quote: முற்பிறப்பின்கண் அன்போடு பொருந்தச் சென்ற செலவென்று சொல்லுவர்

position: The verse is an analogy: love and action should fit as soul and body do.
quote: உயிரும் உடலும்போல் அன்பும் செயலும் இணைந்திருப்பதே உயர்ந்த பொருத்தமாகும்.

position: மறம் is hostile feeling, and love helps remove it when one treats an enemy as a friend.
quote: மறத்தை நீக்குதற்கும் துணையாம்

position: Love also stands by those who do மறம்.
quote: அவ்வன்பு மறஞ் செய்வார்க்குத் துணையாம்,

position: மறம் is heroism, and heroic action is also backed by love.
quote: வீரச் செயல்களுக்கும் அன்பு துணையாகத் திகழ்கிறது

position: This is அறம் personified as a deity, impersonal like the sun, and the loveless soul perishes before it.
quote: அன்பில்லாத உயிரை அறக்கடவுள்.

position: What burns is one's own conscience, in someone who knows virtue but doesn't follow it.
quote: அவரது மனச்சாட்சியே வாட்டி வதைக்கும்.

position: Outer 'parts' are household means such as place, wealth and servants, because the body reading has no connection to household life.
quote: புறத்து உறுப்பாவன: இடனும், பொருளும், ஏவல் செய்வாரும் முதலாயின.

position: Outer parts are the body's beauty, which is pointless without love.
quote: புறத்து உறுப்புகள் அழகாக இருந்து என்ன பயன்?

note: Both say that a living body can be dead in effect, and Manakkudavar on 9 also says such bodies lack life. The criterion is worship in chapter 1 and love in chapter 8, so the two chapters compete for what makes a person alive.

Both picture a bolted door. Love has no bolt here, and in 1251 desire breaks the door of நிறை that shame has barred. The image passes from the ethics of love to its erotic form, with the same result: it won't stay shut in.
This strengthens Kalaignar's reading of 76. In 773, the highest courage is fierce, and its sharp edge is kindness to those in need, so the book elsewhere does join courage to kindness.

position: No sowing is needed, since the field will yield by itself.
quote: 'தானே விளையும்' என்பது குறிப்பெச்சம்.

position: Such a host would use even the seed set aside for the field to feed guests.
quote: தன் நிலத்திற்குரிய விதையைக்கூட விருந்தோம்பலுக்குப் பயன்படுத்தாமல் இருப்பானா?

note: Amrita is beaten twice in these household chapters: a child's stirred gruel is sweeter than it, and even it isn't worth having while a guest waits. In both, food's worth is decided by who else is at the meal.
Both end in the same phrase, வேளாண்மை செய்தற் பொருட்டு: 81 says the home exists for this, and 212 says wealth earned by effort does. Two different goods are given one purpose.

Here refusal of guests is poverty amid plenty. In 1005, someone with crores is destitute if he neither gives nor enjoys. The later verse widens the charge by also treating failure to enjoy one's wealth as a failure.
The anicham measures the guest here and the beloved in 1111, and both are more delicate than it. The book's most tender image for a lover was first used for a stranger at the door.

position: செம்பொருள் is virtue, and the speakers are those who understand it.
quote: அறத்தினை உணர்ந்தார் வாயிற்சொற்கள்.

position: The speakers judge disputes between two parties, and they must rebuke sweetly too.
quote: இஃது ஒருவனைக் கடிந்து சொல்லவேண்டு மிடத்தும் இன்சொல்லாலே கடிய வேண்டுமென்றது.

position: துவ்வாமை is material poverty, in which the senses have nothing to enjoy.
quote: துன்பத்தை மிகுவிக்கும் நல்குரவு இல்லையாம்.

position: The want removed is a poverty of friendship.
quote: 'நட்பில் வறுமை' எனும் துன்பமில்லை.

note: Both use the pair அகனமர்ந்து and முகனமர்ந்து. In 84 the goddess's glad heart answers the host's glad face. In 92 the glad face outranks even the giver's glad heart, so the same pair yields a different ranking.
Sweet words here must be free of deceit. In 292, even a falsehood counts as truth if it yields blameless good. What 91 excludes by definition, 292 may allow when the outcome justifies it.

Here a pleasant word beats a gladly given gift. In 225, relieving hunger is a power above the ascetic's. A hungry person's view of 92 might differ, which suggests the ranking in 92 assumes someone who isn't in need.

Parimelazhagar limits humility in 95 to those who deserve deference. In 125, bowing is good for all and most of all for the rich, which speaks to who should bow rather than to whom, and doesn't contain his limit.
97 requires speech to be useful and gentle, and 200 says to speak only what is useful. The later chapter keeps the usefulness test and drops the sweetness, which shows the two tests are independent.

On Parimelazhagar's reading, 99 argues from how sweet words feel to oneself. 316 makes the same move in general: don't do to others what you know to be painful. The same reciprocity works for speech and for deeds.

position: He reports another reading of the text, about help given to those unable to return it.
quote: மறித்து உதவமாட்டாமை உள்ளவிடத்துச் செய்த உதவி என்று உரைப்பாரும் உளர்.

position: This concerns repayment: what the receiver gives back is measured by the receiver's own worth, not by the original help.
quote: கைம்மாறான உதவி, காரணத்தானும் பொருளானும் காலத்தானும் ஆகிய மூவகையானும் முன் செய்த உதவியளவிற்று அன்று;

position: This concerns the help itself: its value is judged by the quality of whoever receives it.
quote: அந்த உதவியைப் பெறுபவரின் பண்பைப் பொறுத்தே அதன் அளவு மதிப்பிடப்படும்.

position: Seven births are meant literally: affection for the helper carries on in each birth.
quote: பிறப்புதோறும் தொடர்ந்து அன்புடையராதல்.

position: Seven births is a figure of exaggeration meaning that there is no time limit.
quote: மிகைப்படுத்திச் சொல்லுவதுபோல,

position: Even the great crimes, cutting a cow's udder, destroying a womb and killing a Brahmin, can be expiated, as Purananuru 34 lists.
quote: 'ஆன்முலை அறுத்தலும், மகளிர் கருவினைச் சிதைத்தலும், பார்ப்பார்த்தபுதலும்' (புறநா 34)

note: Both use seven births. In 62 a child's character shields the parent, and in 107 memory of a helper persists. Parimelazhagar on 107 refers back to his explanation at 62, so he treats the phrase as one idea.

On Kalaignar's reading of 105, both make the recipient the measure of the gift: the guest's worth in 87 and the helped person's character in 105. Parimelazhagar's different reading of 105 separates them.

Help without weighing the return is vaster than the sea, and in 221 giving outside the destitute is a kind of expected repayment. The two define real generosity by lack of calculation, from the receiver's and the giver's sides.
The same millet and palm. Here others' small kindnesses are enlarged, and in 433 one's own small faults are. The same mental act, turned in opposite directions, gives gratitude and conscience.

position: The parts are enemy, stranger and friend, toward each of whom one keeps the same rule.
quote: பகை, நொதுமல், நட்பு எனும் பகுதிதோறும், தன் முறைமையை விடாது ஒழுகப் பெறின்,

position: The parts are each person's own station, so what is due varies with position.
quote: அவரவர் நிலைமைப்பகுதியோடே அறத்தின் பாற்பட்டு ஒழுகப் பெறுமாயின்,

position: What remains is good offspring, whose presence or absence is a sure mark.
quote: தக்கார்க்கு எச்சம் உண்டாதலும் தகவிலார்க்கு இல்லையாதலும் ஒரு தலையாகலின்,

position: What remains is the praise or blame left after a person is gone.
quote: அவருக்குப் பின் எஞ்சி நிற்கப் போகும் புகழ்ச் சொல்லைக் கொண்டோ அல்லது பழிச் சொல்லைக் கொண்டோதான்

position: They are already laid down by past deeds, so bending to get or avoid them achieves nothing.
quote: 'அவற்றிற்குக் காரணம் பழவினையே; கோடுதல் அன்று'

position: Rise and fall are simply the nature of the world.
quote: ஒருவர்க்கு வாழ்வும், தாழ்வும் உலக இயற்கை;

note: 112 promises that a fair person's wealth will last, and 117 allows that such a person may fall into low estate. The chapter keeps both. The second stops the first from being a simple reward promise.
Gain got by leaving what is fair should be given up, and in 657 even extreme poverty is better for the worthy than wealth got through blame. The later verse states the cost openly.

On Parimelazhagar's reading, both rest on past deeds, and each draws a response. 379 asks why one grieves at the bad after accepting the good, and 115 asks that one's heart not bend. The first is about feeling and the second about justice.

Parimelazhagar takes 116 to mean that thinking equals doing, and 282 says outright that even thinking of stealing another's goods is wrong. This suggests that the Kural's standard really does reach into thought.

position: The destinations are literal: the gods' world and a particular hell called darkness.
quote: 'இருள்' என்பது ஓர் நரக விசேடம்.

position: The results are this-worldly: lasting renown and a darkened life.
quote: அடக்கம் அழியாத புகழைக் கொடுக்கும். அடங்காமை வாழ்வையே இருளாக்கி விடும்.

position: The station is household life, and the restraint is exercised while enjoying sense objects.
quote: பொறிகளால் புலன்களை நுகராநின்றே அடங்குதல்.

position: The station is the order of varna and stage of life.
quote: நிலை - வன்னாச்சிரம தன்மம்.

position: It's a matter of firmness of mind joined to unostentatious restraint.
quote: உறுதியான உள்ளமும், அத்துடன் ஆர்ப்பாட்டமற்ற அடக்க உணர்வும்

position: One harm caused by evil words turns the good of the speaker's other virtues to evil.
quote: அவனுக்குப் பிற அறங்களான் உண்டான நன்மை தீதாய்விடும்.

position: It concerns a word sweet to the hearer but harmful in effect, so flattery is also bad.
quote: இது சால மொழி கூறினாலுந் தீதாமென்றது.

position: One bad word in a speech spoils all of that speech's good words, like poison in milk.
quote: ஒரு குடம் பாலில் துளி நஞ்சுபோல்,

note: The five senses are imagined as animals in both cases. In 24 they're elephants controlled by a goad, and in 126 they're a tortoise's limbs drawn in. One is control by force and the other is retreat to safety.

The renouncer quenches the five in 25. In 124, on Parimelazhagar's reading, the householder is restrained while enjoying the senses and is also called greater than a mountain. They are two different pictures of what restraint is.

Both say that no gain surpasses this, in the same formula (ஊங்கு), but 32 says it of virtue and 122 of restraint. The superlatives compete, as also in 61 on children, which suggests that the formula praises and doesn't actually rank.

In both அறம் acts like a person, and Parimelazhagar calls it a deity in both. In 77 it burns the loveless like the sun, and here it waits for the restrained like a petitioner. It's the same power with opposite manners.

Harsh speech in 100 is merely a stupid choice of raw fruit. In 129 it leaves a scar that never heals. The first chapter on speech treats the speaker's loss, and this one treats the listener's lasting injury.

In 109 one good act erases even murderous harm. In 128 one bad word turns all good to nothing. The ledgers are asymmetric, though the verses keep different books: the first is the recipient's memory, and the second, in Parimelazhagar's reading, is the speaker's merit.

position: Status really changes: a low-born person of good conduct becomes high, and a high-born person who fails falls.
quote: உயர்ந்த வருணத்துப் பிறந்தாராயினும் ஒழுக்கத்தில் தவறத் தாழ்ந்த வருணத்தராவர்

position: Conduct is the evidence of good birth, and failures are regarded as low-born whoever they are.
quote: ஒழுக்கம் தவறுகிறவர்கள் யாவராயினும் அவர்கள் இழிந்த குடியில் பிறந்தவர்களாகவே கருதப்படுவர்.

position: When enemies make false charges, the world believes them because of the earlier lapse.
quote: பகை பற்றி அடாப்பழி கூறியவழி, அதனையும் இழுக்கம்பற்றி உலகம் அடுக்கும் என்று கொள்ளுமாகலின்,

position: Living with the world includes setting aside what the moral texts say that doesn't suit this age, and taking up what suits it.
quote: அறநூல் சொல்லியவற்றுள் இக்காலத்திற்கு ஏலாதன ஒழிந்து, சொல்லாதனவற்றுள் ஏற்பன கொண்டு வருதலான்

note: The two ask the same question, what learning is worth, and answer differently. For 2, learning lacks fruit without worship, and for 140 it isn't understanding without fitting conduct in the world. One looks up and the other looks out.
131 places conduct above life in general. 327 gives a specific case: don't take another's life, even at the cost of your own. It shows what 'guarding it above life' can literally mean.

Both separate social rank from worth. 133 says this of conduct and birth, and 973 goes further with the high who aren't high and the low who aren't low. Read together, they show a repeated Kural challenge to status by birth.
Both tie understanding to how the world lives. Verse 426 calls it அறிவு to live as the world lives, which is a striking statement beside Parimelazhagar's narrowing of 'world' to the noble in 140.

Parimelazhagar uses Indra to illustrate both verses: 25 for the failure that shows the ascetic's power, and 144 for greatness lost through another's wife. This is one story serving two chapters in the commentary, though neither verse tells it.

Both call a living person effectively dead. In 80 it's the lack of love, and in 143, as both early commentators say, it's the loss of all three aims. A person can stop being alive in more than one way.

These are the two 'at least this' verses: however much else is left unguarded, guard the tongue; however wrong the rest, don't desire another's wife. They show what the book treats as the last line of moral defence.
Both define பேராண்மை, the same word. In 773 it is ferocity in battle whose edge is kindness, and here it is not looking at another's wife. The book redefines the warrior's virtue as self-mastery.

position: விருந்து means a guest, and turning one away is the worst poverty.
quote: வறுமையுள் வைத்து வறுமையாவது விருந்தினரை ஏற்றுக் கொள்ளாது நீக்குதல்;

position: விருந்து means novelty: the weakest weakness is failing to reject the strange and unheard-of.
quote: புதுமை யென்றது கேட்டறியாதது.

position: The word 'world' is supplied, so the renown lasts until the world itself ends.
quote: பொறுத்தார்க்கு உலகம் அழியுமளவும் புகழ் உண்டாம்.

position: The renown lasts as long as the forbearing person lives.
quote: பொறுத்த வர்க்குத் தாம் சாமளவும் புகழுண்டாம்,

position: One grieves for the suffering that will come to the wrongdoer, who may fall into hell.
quote: அவர்க்கு அதனால் வரும் துன்பத்திற்கு நொந்து,

position: One feels hurt by the base act done to oneself, and still does not take revenge.
quote: பிறர் செய்திடும் இழிவான காரியங்களுக்காகத் துன்பமுற்று வருந்தி;

note: Both set a kind of endurance above the ascetic's. 48 says the householder endures more because he also bears others' pain, and 160 says that bearing harsh words comes first. Each reassigns the word நோன்பு or நோன்மை to a life in society.

நிறை appears in 57 as a woman's inner guard, and here it's what anyone stands to lose without forbearance. The same inner discipline is asked of women as chastity and of people in general as character.
Both call refusal of a guest a kind of poverty. 89 says so directly, and 153 uses it as an analogy for something else, which shows that this was a settled saying that could be drawn on.

Both say that forgetting is what's best. On Parimelazhagar's reading of 108 it's narrowly about one who has also done good. Verse 152 removes that limit, and gives forgetting a rank above forbearance.
157 asks for not retaliating, and 314 goes further: punish the wrongdoer by doing him good so that he's ashamed. What starts as restraint becomes a strategy.

Two verses, for different reasons, place the ascetic's hunger second. In 160 it's after bearing insults, and in 225 it's after relieving others' hunger. The book keeps finding what's greater than fasting.

position: The goddess too can't bear it, and leaves after showing him to her elder sister.
quote: திருமகள் தானும் பொறாது, தன் தவ்வைக்கு காட்டி நீங்கும்.

position: These results can't come from crookedness or uprightness, so the wise ask what past deed caused them.
quote: 'இதற்கு ஏது ஆகிய பழவினை யாது?' என்று ஆராயப்படுதலின்,

position: This is simply a matter for astonishment, with no appeal to past deeds.
quote: வியப்புக்குரிய செய்தியாகும்.

note: The same goddess. She settles gladly in the home of the glad-faced host in 84, and here she hands the envious to her sister. Fortune is given a personality that responds to moral character.

This is Parimelazhagar's own cross-reference. He cites 166 to read 135's simile: as the envious man's kin suffer, so do a man's kin when he lacks conduct. The commentary reads one verse by way of the other.

The same logic is used in two domains: the passion is its own executioner. Envy needs no enemies, and in 305 anger left unguarded kills its owner. The book treats inner states as weapons pointed inward.

169 says that the crooked prosper and the upright fall, and that this should be pondered. Then 170 says that it never happens. The two stand side by side, which suggests that 170 is a moral claim and that 169 knows what experience shows.

Both admit that outcomes don't track merit. 375 says so within the chapter on fate, and 169 only asks for thought, though Parimelazhagar explains it through past deeds. The tension in chapter 38 is here in an earlier and quieter form.

position: The other joy is the lasting joy that comes from virtue.
quote: அறத்தான் வரும் நிலையுடைய இன்பத்தைக் காதலிப்பவர்.

position: The other joy is the great joy of release.
quote: பேரின்பமாகிய வீடுபேற்றைக் காமிப்பவர்,

position: It's a lasting benefit that one wants in place of an immediate one.
quote: அறவழியில் நிலையான பயனை விரும்புகிறவர்

position: The path is household life, called a path because one can't renounce until understanding matures in it.
quote: இல்லற நெறியில் அறிவு முதிர்ந்துழி அல்லது துறக்கப் படாமையின், அதனைத் துறவறத்திற்கு 'ஆறு' என்றார்.

position: The path is simply the way of virtue, and even one with grace can fall.
quote: அருளை விரும்பி யறனெறியிலே நின்றவனும்,

note: In 39, joy comes only from virtue. Here that claim is put to work: the 'small joy' of taking others' goods is set against a greater one, and on Parimelazhagar's reading, the greater is the same joy of virtue as 39.

In 46 there's nothing to gain by leaving household life. Parimelazhagar on 176 calls household life a path toward renunciation, so leaving is the natural end. This commentator's way of ordering the stages conflicts with the plain force of 46.
Both promise that wealth lasts on a moral condition: fairness in 112 and not coveting in 178. The second is the first's inward side, since 171 treats coveting as itself a lapse from fairness.

Virtue in 130 and fortune in 179 both seek out the right person, and they look for the right moment to do so. Parimelazhagar uses செவ்வி in both notes. Moral power is pictured as a courtier waiting for an opening.
Not wanting yields victory here, and in 363 it's the choicest wealth in this world and the next. Chapter 18 is about not wanting others' goods, and 363 extends this to not wanting at all.

position: The forbidden word disregards the harm that will come later, in the person's absence.
quote: அவன் எதிரின்றிப்பின் வரும் குற்றத்தை நோக்காத சொல்லைச் சொல்லாதொழிக.

position: The forbidden word is one that will leave you unable to look the person in the eye later.
quote: பிற்காலத்து அவன் முன்னே நின்று எதிர்முகம் நோக்க வொண் ணாத சொல்லைச் சொல்லா தொழிக,

position: Seeing the fault ends it, so there's no sin, and thus no suffering in the births to come.
quote: கண்டவழி ஒழிதலின் பாவம் இன்றாம், ஆகவே வரும் பிறவிகளினும் துன்பம் இல்லை என்பது நோக்கி,

position: The habit of backbiting goes and one's life becomes peaceful.
quote: புறங்கூறும் பழக்கமும் போகும்; வாழ்க்கையும் நிம்மதியாக அமையும்.

note: 34 says that a clean mind is all of virtue and the rest is noise. 185 supplies the test: if you can't tell whether the mind behind fine moral talk is clean, listen to how the person speaks of others.
100 calls harsh speech a foolish choice when sweet words are available. 184 ranks it above backbiting. The two together suggest a scale of speech: sweet, then harsh and open, then hidden.

These are built on the same frame: though one does no virtue and does wrong, at least this one thing. The verses name different things, chastity toward others' wives and not backbiting, so the 'last virtue' isn't a single item.

The earth is the model of forbearance in 151, holding up those who dig it. Here it has to talk itself into bearing the backbiter. This suggests that the backbiter does what digging doesn't: he tests even the earth's patience.

Both pick out the false smile. In 182 it's the worst part of backbiting, and in 824 the sweet-smiling face over a bitter heart is to be feared. The moral judgment in chapter 19 becomes a practical warning in the book on friendship.

These share the word காண்கிற்பின் and the same question about faults. In 190 any person who sees his own faults is safe from harm. In 436 a king who has removed his own and then looks at others' has no fault left. The same self-scrutiny serves an ordinary person and a ruler.

position: The words fall short of justice toward the listeners, and cost the speaker his good qualities.
quote: அவை அவர்மாட்டு நீதியோடு படாவாய், அவனை நற்குணங்களின் நீக்கும்.

position: நயன் is even-handedness, and it is the speaker who loses that balance and falls from goodness.
quote: அவன் நடு சாராது நன்மையி னீங்கும்

position: நயன் is the gladness of the gathering, and such words destroy it along with good.
quote: மகிழ்ச்சியைக் குலைத்து, நன்மையை மாய்க்கும்.

position: பாராட்டுவான் is one who says such things repeatedly: the fault is the habit.
quote: பயன் இல்லாத சொற்களைப் பலகாலுஞ் சொல்லுவானை

position: He is one who prizes and celebrates useless speech: the fault is the relish.
quote: பயனில்லாத சொல்லைக் கொண்டாடுவானை

position: He is one who hopes to profit from empty talk: the fault is the motive.
quote: பயனற்றவைகளைச் சொல்லிப் பயன்பெற நினைப்பவனை

position: நயன் is justice, so even speech at odds with justice is ranked less bad than useless speech.
quote: நயன் இலவற்றினும் பயன் இல தீய என்பதாம்.

position: நயன் is pleasantness, so the worthy may say what is unsweet, which is a much milder claim.
quote: பண்பாளர்கள், இனிமையல்லாத சொற்களைக்கூடச் சொல்லி விடலாம்;

position: The rare ends are release and passage to higher worlds.
quote: அறிதற்கு அரிய பயன்களாவன: வீடு பேறும் மேற்கதிச் செலவும் முதலாயின.

position: சொல்லில் means 'among words': the verse sorts words into two kinds.
quote: சொற்களில் பயன் உடைய சொற்களைச் சொல்லுக

position: The first சொல்லில் means 'if you speak', which leaves silence as an option.
quote: சொல்லுவனாயின் பயனுடைய சொற்களைச் சொல்லுக

note: 100 calls harsh speech a raw fruit taken over a ripe one, yet on Kalaignar's reading 197 tolerates unsweet speech before useless speech. Sweetness is not the highest test of a word.
291 defines truthfulness as speech without harm; 200 demands use. Harmless idle talk passes the one test and fails the other, so the two chapters set different standards for speech.
645 echoes the same imperative and raises the standard: useful is not enough if some other word could defeat it.
Both deny full humanity by appearance alone: chaff has the look of grain, and the base look like people. For the Kural, being human is something a person can fail at.
Both use 'even by forgetting', 199 for the speech of the clear-sighted and 204 for plotting harm. The first describes an achieved nature, and the second commands what such a nature would be.

position: செருக்கு is delusion: the evil deed is called by the name of the confusion it brings on.
quote: தீவினை என்று சொல்லப்படும் மயக்கத்தை

position: செருக்கு is the elation of wrongdoing.
quote: தீவினை யாகிய களிப்பை

position: செருக்கு is a pleasure the deed may yield, and the wise fear the deed even so.
quote: தீவினையால் மகிழ்ச்சி ஏற்படுவதாயினும்

position: Fire can't burn in another time, another place or another body, and an evil deed can.
quote: பிறிதொரு காலத்தும், பிறிதொரு தேயத்தும், பிறிதோர் உடம்பினும் சென்று சுடுதல் தீக்கு இன்மையின்

position: It is the chief understanding because one infers that refraining, even when able to strike, keeps suffering away.
quote: செய்யத் தக்குழியுஞ் செய்யாது ஒழியவே தமக்குத் துன்பம் வாராது என உய்த்துணர்தலின்

position: அறம் is a deity of virtue, and its 'plotting' is resolving to leave the man to his ruin.
quote: அறக்கடவுள் எண்ணுதலாவது, அவன் கெடத் தான் நீங்க நினைத்தல்.

position: அறம் actively returns harm for harm, and gets in before the intended victim can respond.
quote: தீமை செய்தார்க்குத் தீமை பயக்கும் அறந்தானே சூழும்

position: சூழும் means surrounds: moral order closes in on him like a siege.
quote: அவனுக்குக் கேடு உண்டாக்க அவனை அறம் முற்றுகையிட்டு விடும்.

position: The poverty returns across lives, birth after birth.
quote: அத் தீவினையால் பிறவிதோறும் இலன் ஆம் என்பதாம்.

position: The deed simply fails to produce wealth, with no appeal to rebirth.
quote: பின்பும் நல்குரவினனாவன்; அது செல் வம் பயவாது

position: The image is the shadow's return to the foot, not a deed lying hidden until its season.
quote: ஒருவன் நிழல் நொடிதாகப் போயும், அவன்றன்னை விடாது வந்து அடியின்கண் தங்கி தன்மைத்து.

position: அருமை means absence, so the man has no ruin at all.
quote: அருமை:இன்மை.

note: 201 makes fear the mark of the excellent; 1075 makes fear the conduct of the base. They can be reconciled only by asking what is feared, which suggests that fear of the deed and fear of the penalty are morally different things.
203 only asks one to refrain from harming an enemy. 314 goes further and makes kindness to the wrongdoer the punishment itself. Prudent restraint becomes active shaming.

205 argues that wrongdoing won't cure poverty. 657 removes that premise: even when wealth does come through blame, the poverty of the worthy is better. Moral refusal doesn't depend on the prediction in 205.
They give the same rule different grounds. 206 rests on what will come back to you, 316 on knowing from your own experience what hurts. One argues from consequence and the other from fellow-feeling.
Two pursuers that can't be evaded: the deed follows from behind (பின் சென்று) and fate arrives first (முந்துறும்). Together they close off escape in both directions.
Both turn on தன்னைத்தான், making care for the self the argument for restraint: from evil deeds here, from anger in 305.
210 says the upright man's ruin is absent or rare. 169 admits that this ruin does occur and is something to ponder. The Kural keeps the moral promise and the troubling fact side by side.

position: தக்கார் are the owners: for those who are worthy, all wealth is for benevolence, not for private consumption or hoarding.
quote: தக்கார்க்கு தகுதி உடையார்க்கு ஆயின்;

position: தக்கார் are the recipients: the wealth is for helping those who deserve it.
quote: ஒருவன் முயன்று ஈட்டிய பொருளெல்லாம் தகுதியுடையார்க்கு உபகரித்தற்காகவாம்

position: புத்தேள் உலகு is the world of the gods.
quote: தேவர் உலகத்தும் இவ்வுலகத்தும்

position: It is a new world yet to come, which removes the gods from the verse.
quote: இன்றைய உலகிலும், இனிவரும் புதிய உலகிலும் காண்பது அரிது.

position: What is fitting is the way of the world as a whole, and lapses in it can't be repaired as lapses in Vedic practice can.
quote: உலகநடை வழு வேதநடை வழுப்போலத் தீர்திறன் உடைத்து அன்று

position: What is fitting is specifically ஒப்புரவு, and those who lack it are like corpses.
quote: ஒப்புரவறியாதார் பிணத்தோ டொப்ப ரென்றது.

position: This person desires and practises the world's way.
quote: உலகநடையை விரும்பிச் செய்யும் பெரிய அறிவினை யுடையவனது செல்வம்

position: This person is the one desired by all the world.
quote: உலகத்தா ரெல்லாராலும் நச்சப்படுகின்ற

position: Selling oneself is meant literally as the limit case: the loss is worth buying even at that price.
quote: அக்கேடு தன்னை விற்றாயினும் கொள்ளும் தகுதியை உடைத்து.

position: It is a commercial image, selling one thing to obtain another, so the 'loss' is really a trade for later benefit.
quote: ஒன்றை விற்று ஒன்றைக் கொள்ளுகின்ற வாணிகமாகக் கொள்ளுந் தகுதி புடைத்து

note: 211 insists that obligation looks for no return. 226 commends feeding the destitute as the place to store one's wealth, and Parimelazhagar says it comes back to help the giver. One motive disclaims reward and the other promises it.

An exact inversion: the same tree in mid-town, same ripening. In 216 it bears useful fruit; in 1008 it is a poison tree. The chapters on benevolence and on useless wealth share one picture, and only the owner's character changes it.
Both move the definition of being alive from body to relationship: 80 to love, 214 to knowing what is due. The body without these is bone and skin, or a corpse.
219 says the good man's poverty is being unable to give. 230 pushes this further: being unable to give makes even death sweet.
220 only says that ruin from generosity is worth buying. 235 takes up the same word and explains how there can be a ruin that is a gain, and says that only the skilled achieve it.

position: Both 'even ifs' are purely hypothetical: no one actually says such things, and heaven isn't in doubt.
quote: 'எனினும்' என்பது இரு வழியும் அங்ஙனம் கூறுவார் இன்மை விளக்கி நின்றது.

position: Giving won't obtain any higher world, and the giving life is best regardless.
quote: கொடை வழங்குவதால் மேலுலகம் என்று சொல்லப்படுவது கிட்டிவிடப் போவதில்லை;

position: These are two virtues: not begging oneself, and not refusing those who beg.
quote: யான் வறியன் என்று இரப்பான் சொல்லும் இளிவரவைத் தான் பிறர்கண் சொல்லாமையும்

position: It is one act: giving without telling the suppliant 'I have nothing'.
quote: இரந்து வந்தார்க்கு இல னென்னாகின்ற துன்பத்தைக் கூறாது ஈதலும்

position: It means giving without showing the distress of one's own poverty.
quote: தமக்குள்ள வறுமைத் துன்பத்தைக் காட்டிக்கொள்ளாமல் பிறருக்கு ஈவது

position: இரக்கப்படுதல் is being the one asked, and resolving to give.
quote: இரக்கப்படுதல்-'இரப்பார்க்கு ஈவல்' என்று இருத்தல்.

position: It is feeling pity (இரக்கம்) for the supplicant, a different root.
quote: அவருக்காக இரக்கப்படுவதும் ஒரு துன்பமாகவே தோன்றும்.

position: It answers the fear that giving will reduce wealth and bring on hunger.
quote: பகுத்துண்ணப் பசி வாராதென்று கூறிற்று.

position: நிரப்பிய refers to filling a fixed hoard target, so the fault is accumulation.
quote: ஒரோ எண்களைக்குறித்து அத்துணை ஈட்டுதும் என ஈட்டத்தையே மேற்கொண்டு இவறக் கூட்டுதல்.

position: It refers to the food one has obtained, and தமியர் to eating out of everyone's sight.
quote: தேடின வுணவைத தாமே தமியராயிருந் துண்டல்

note: On Manakkudavar's reading of 212, wealth is for helping those who deserve it. 221 says that true giving goes to those who lack. The worthy recipient and the needy recipient are different tests, and these chapters leave both standing.

222 calls taking bad even if it were a path to heaven. 1051 permits begging from the right people and puts any blame on the one who refuses. The chapters on giving and begging judge the same act from different standpoints.

229 names something worse than begging; 1066 says that nothing disgraces the tongue more than begging, even for a cow's water. Their standards differ: the misery of a life against the shame of an act.
225 places enduring hunger below removing it. 261 defines austerity as endurance plus not harming living things, so the austerity that 225 ranks low is not the fuller ideal of chapter 27.
228 asks whether hoarders know the joy they forfeit. 1001 gives the outcome: he dies without eating what he amassed, and nothing remains to be done with it.

position: புலவர் are sages who have reached that world, and it prefers the famous to them.
quote: புத்தேள் உலகம் அவனையல்லது தன்னை எய்தி நின்ற ஞானிகளைப் பேணாது.

position: புலவர் are the gods themselves, so named because they have wisdom.
quote: புலவரென்றார் தேவரை; அவர் புலனுடையாராதலான்.

position: புலவர் are the learned and the world is a future one: it will not honour intellect alone over the selfless and famous.
quote: அறிவாற்றல் உடையவரை மட்டும் போற்றிக் கொண்டிராது.

position: It is a doctrine of two bodies: the elemental body grows poor and dies while the body of fame grows rich and stands.
quote: ஆக்கமாகும் கேடாவது, புகழ் உடம்பு செல்வம் எய்தப் பூத உடம்பு நல்கூர்தல்.

position: It speaks of strength of character that grows fame amid hardship and establishes it even in dying, with no second body.
quote: துன்பங்களுக்கிடையேகூட அவற்றைத் தாங்கும் வலிமையால் தமது புகழை வளர்த்துக் கொள்வதும்,

position: It means being born human, and for those lacking the qualities that lead to fame, an animal birth is better, since no one reviles animals.
quote: அக்குணம் இல்லாதார் மக்களாய்ப் பிறத்தலின் விலங்காய்ப் பிறத்தல் நன்று.

position: It means plainly that not being born is better.
quote: அஃதிலார் பிறக்குமதிற் பிறவாமை நன்று

position: தோன்று means entering a field of activity: excel there, or stay out of it.
quote: எந்தத் துறையில் ஈடுபட்டாலும் அதில் புகழுடன் விளங்கவேண்டும்;

note: 233 names renown as the one thing in the world that doesn't die. 331 calls taking what doesn't last for what lasts the lowest kind of knowledge. Chapter 34 never excepts fame, so fame's permanence is exactly what the later chapter puts in doubt.
222 calls giving good even with no reward in any world. 231 calls giving, with renown, the sole profit of a life. The same act is valued for itself in one and as a gain in the other.
Both rest on எச்சம், what is left behind. 114 reads a person's worth from what remains after them, and 238 makes renown the remainder that everyone should leave.
The earth is morally responsive in both: it yields less under a body without fame, and laughs at those who sit idle pleading poverty. Land is more than a backdrop to human conduct in the Kural.
The same reclassification of the living as dead, with different tests: renown in 240, knowing what is due in 214. The chapters on benevolence and fame are linked as cause and result.

position: Mutually opposed schools agree on this one point.
quote: அன்னவாயினும், அருள் துணை என்றற்கண் ஒக்கும் என்பதாம்.

position: It is a literal hell, a place in the lower world.
quote: தன்கண்ணே புக்கார்க்குத் துன்பம் செய்வதோர் நரகத்தை

position: The darkness is ignorance, and the suffering is of this life.
quote: அறியாமை எனும் இருள் சூழ்ந்த துன்ப உலகில்

position: பொருள் is virtue: they failed to practise it before and have forgotten the suffering they are in as a result.
quote: முன்னும் உறுதிப் பொருளைச் செய்யாது தாம் துன்புறுகின்றமையை மறந்தவர்

position: பொருள் is wealth, and the verse spans lives: lacking அருள் in a former birth, they are now both poor and forgetful.
quote: இப்பிறப்பின்கண் பொருளினின்று நீங்கி மறவியு முடையவ

position: With no former birth in view, the cruel become poor and forget their duty.
quote: பொருளற்றவர்களாகவும், கடமை மறந்தவர்களாகவும் ஆவர்.

position: That world is release.
quote: உயிர்கள்மேல் அருள் இல்லாதார்க்கு வீட்டுலகத்து இன்பம் இல்லை

position: That world is heaven.
quote: இஃது அருளில்லாதார் சுவர்க்கம் புகாரென்றது.

position: It isn't another world at all: wealth is to the household life as compassion is to the renouncer's life.
quote: கருணை உள்ளம் இல்லாதவர்களின் துறவற வாழ்க்கையும் சிறப்பாக அமையாது.

position: Such virtue can occur, as a passing glimpse can, but the person's own lack destroys it.
quote: அருளாதான் இடையே அறஞ்செய்தால் அதனைத் தன் அருளாமையால் தானே அழித்துவிடும்

position: Such people can't practise virtue at all.
quote: இஃது அறஞ்செய்யவும் மாட்டாரென்றது,

note: The same formula, செல்வத்துட் செல்வம், crowns different things: அருள் here and hearing in 411. Both can't be 'the' wealth of wealths unless the phrase is a rhetorical form awarded in context, a caution against reading any single chapter as the Kural's ultimate ranking.

247 mentions as an aside that this world is not for the penniless. 751 makes that its full subject: nothing but wealth makes nobodies into somebodies. The section on virtue quietly grants the premise of the section on wealth.

248 says those without அருள் are finished and can't become anything. 250, which Parimelazhagar calls the means of arousing அருள், assumes that the person going against the weak can still acquire it. The verdict is absolute, and the very next step offers a way out.
34 says stainlessness of mind is the whole of virtue and all else is show. 249 makes the same point about compassion: an outwardly right act without it does not count.

Both derive compassion from one's own experience: 250 remembers fear before the strong, and 318 asks how one who knows pain in his own life could inflict it. The Kural's ethics of harm consistently starts from self-knowledge and not from rules.

position: The verse rebuts the claim that good intention makes flesh-eating harmless to அருள்.
quote: ஊன் தின்றாராயினும் உயிர்கட்கு ஒரு தீங்கும் நினையாதார்க்கு அருள் ஆள்தற்கு இழுக்கு இல்லை என்பாரை மறுத்து,

position: அருள் is not killing and its opposite is killing, and பொருள் here means virtue, so eating is sin. He also reports another division of the words.
quote: அக்கோறலான் வந்த ஊனைத் தின்கை பாவம்.

position: Non-அருள் is destroying the vow of not killing, and பொருள் means gain, so eating harms அருள் and gets one nothing.
quote: அருள் கெடுதலேயன்றி, பெறுவதொரு பயனுமில்லை என்றது.

position: It answers those who ask what fault there is in buying and eating without having killed.
quote: கொன்று தின்னாது விலைக்குக் கொண்டு தின்பார்க்குக் குற்றமென்னை யென்றார்க்கு , அதனாலுங் கொலைப்பாவம் வருமென்று கூறிற்று.

note: 253 uses the weapon-holder as the model of a mind closed to good. 774 celebrates a warrior who plucks a spear from his own body and laughs. The Kural honours in the section on polity the same figure that it distrusts in the section on virtue.
329 condemns killers as base. 256 extends the guilt to the customer who keeps them in business, so the customer can't look down on the butcher.

Both move the worth of sacrifice elsewhere: 88 calls hospitality the வேள்வி that misers miss, and 259 ranks not killing above a thousand sacrifices. The Kural repeatedly tests ritual by how others are treated.

Nearly the same ending: all living beings worship. In 260 the object is one who doesn't kill and doesn't eat flesh; in 268 it is one who has mastered, or on another reading lost, his own self. One route looks outward and the other inward.

position: One needs தவம் from an earlier birth, which gives the familiarity needed to complete it.
quote: தவந்தானும் உண்டாவது முன்தவம் உடையார்க்கே

position: It requires earlier good deeds of any kind, not earlier austerity as such.
quote: தவஞ்செய்தலும் முன்பு நல்வினை செய்தார்க்கு வரும்

position: It requires present firmness and self-control, with no former birth involved.
quote: உறுதிப்பாடும், மன அடக்கமும் உடையவருக்கே தவத்தின் பெருமை வாய்க்கும்.

position: Householders, drawn by love of giving, have forgotten what is greater.
quote: தானத்தினும் தவம் மிக்கது என்பது பெற்றாம்.

position: The foes are enemies of virtue, and the friends are those who delight in it.
quote: அறத்திற்குப் பகையாய் அழிவு செய்தாரைக் கெடுத்தலும்

position: These are ordinary enemies and friends, and the power comes from austerity done earlier.
quote: பகைவரைத் தெறுதலும், நட்டோரையாக்குதலு மாகிய வலி ஆராயின், முன்செய்த தவத்தினாலே வரும்

position: He has obtained his own self as truly his own, and அற intensifies this: nothing is harder to obtain.
quote: தன் உயிரைத் தான் தனக்கு உரித்தாகப் பெற்றவனை

position: அற marks cessation: he has got rid of the thought of 'I', and தான் is the ego.
quote: தானறு தலாவது அகங்கார மறு தல்.

position: He has neither attachment to 'my life' nor the pride of 'I'.
quote: "தனது உயிர்" என்கிற பற்றும், "தான்" என்கிற செருக்கும் கொள்ளாதவர்களை

position: Wealth and poverty here include having and lacking understanding.
quote: செல்வம் நல்குரவு என்பன ஈண்டு அறிவினது உண்மை இன்மைகளையும் குறித்து நின்றன;

position: It is about those without goods, plainly.
quote: பொருளில்லாதார் உலகத்துப் பலராதற்குக் காரணம், தவஞ் செய்வார் சிலராதல்;

position: It is about those lacking capability, and the few are simply those with firm resolve.
quote: ஆற்றலற்றவர்கள் பலராக இருப்பதற்குக் காரணம், மன உறுதி கொண்டவர் சிலராக இருப்பதும்

note: 225 puts the strength of enduring hunger behind that of removing it, which favours the giver. Parimelazhagar and Manakkudavar draw from 263 that தவம் exceeds giving. Whatever the verses themselves imply, the commentary tradition faces a real conflict here.

203 calls refraining from harm even to enemies the height of understanding, and 261 defines austerity by harmlessness. Yet 264 advertises the power to crush foes. Parimelazhagar's 'enemies of virtue' and his comment that ascetics don't think of it are attempts to close this gap.

46 asks what a virtuous householder could gain by leaving for the other path. 266 says that those not doing தவம் are doing futile things. The chapters on householding and austerity each claim the highest place.
265 recommends austerity because it gets whatever one wants. 370 says the unchanging state comes from removing desire. The means is sold by appeal to the very thing the end abolishes.
On Manakkudavar's reading of 268, its subject has lost the ego, which is exactly the cutting of 'I' and 'mine' in 346. Parimelazhagar's 'possessing oneself' would make the link weaker.

Two different conquests of death: by the power of austerity in 269, and by the vow of not killing in 326, where death's advance doesn't reach. The Kural offers an ethical route alongside the ascetic one.
270 explains poverty as too little austerity, which is something people could change. 377 says enjoyment is only as the apportioner apportioned. The same fact gets a moral cause and a fatal one.

position: The elements themselves are the cosmic witnesses, mingled in his body and laughing without his knowing.
quote: உடம்பாய் அவனோடு கலந்து நிற்கின்ற பூதங்கள் ஐந்தும் கண்டு தம்முள்ளே நகும்.

position: 'Elements' stands for the senses, their products, which know what he does.
quote: பூதங்களென்றது அவையிற்றின் காரியமாகிய பொறிகளை .

position: The cry belongs to the hypocrites, who later lament what they have done.
quote: பின் 'என் செய்தோம்! என் செய்தோம்! என்று தாமே இரங்கும்வகை,

position: The cry belongs to everyone, who exclaim at such a person, and எற்று is a regional word.
quote: எல்லாரும் எற்றெற்றென்று சொல்லும்படி பலகுற்றமும் உண்டாக்கும்,

position: They harm those who feed them, since gifts to the unrestrained bring donors a low birth.
quote: தமக்கு ஆவன செய்தார்க்கு ஆகாதன விளைத்தலின் 'வன்கணார் இல்' என்றார்.

position: They literally bathe, to appear distinguished by austerity, and hide behind this.
quote: பிறர்க்குத் தவத்தான் மாட்சிமையுடையராய் நீரின் மூழ்கிக் காட்டி;

position: நீராடி isn't bathing: they put on the நீர்மை, the nature, of the distinguished.
quote: மாட்சிமைப் பட்டாரது நீர்மையைப் பூண்டு,

position: Water is an analogy: they hide under the name of greatness as a diver hides under water.
quote: நீருக்குள் மூழ்கியோர் தம்மை மறைத்துக் கொள்வது போல,

note: Both make one's own heart the witness: 272 says that an outward show can't help when the heart knows the fault, and 293 says the heart will burn the one who lies against what it knows. Self-knowledge is the Kural's court of last resort.
278's மனத்தது மாசாக is the exact opposite of 34's மனத்துக்கண் மாசிலன். 34 states the principle that all else is show, and 278 gives the social picture of the show in practice.

827 warns that a bowing enemy's words are like a bow's bend, which signals harm. 279 says the lute's curve is straight and the arrow's straightness is cruel. So the curve is a warning in one verse and no evidence at all in the other, which supports 279's point that shape can't be read directly.

The same utterance appears in both: in 88, the miser who fed no guests later says பற்றற்றேம் as a lament for lost support, and in 275 the hypocrite says it as a boast of non-attachment. Both are words that the speaker's life makes hollow.

position: It means not scorning release: the person wants liberation and is respected by ascetics for that.
quote: வீட்டினை இகழாது விரும்புவான் இவன் என்று தவத்தோரான் நன்கு மதிக்கப்படுவான்;

position: It means not being scorned by other people, a matter of ordinary repute.
quote: பிறரா லிகழப்படாமையை வேண்டுவா னிவனென்று சொல் லப்படுமவன்,

position: அளவு is reasoned inquiry measuring the soul, karma and release, which he identifies with a Jain term.
quote: உயிர் முதலியவற்றை அளத்தலாகிய நெற்றியின்கண் நின்று அதற்கு ஏற்ப ஒழுகமாட்டார்;

position: அளவு is simply rectitude.
quote: களவின்கண்ணே மிக்க ஆசையையுடையவர் நேரின் கணின்று ஒழுகுதலைச் செய்யமாட்டார்,

position: அளவு is living within limits, and failing to do so leads to theft, which reverses the causal direction.
quote: ஓர் எல்லைக்குட்பட்டு வாழ்வைச் செம்மையாக அமைத்துக் கொள்ளாதவர்கள்,

position: The ruin is immediate and inward: they are lost the moment they think such thoughts, and 'other things' are the renunciant's permitted food and lay gifts.
quote: அவ்வளவல்லாத தீய நினைவுகளை நினைத்த பொழுதே கெடுவர்;

position: The ruin is civil: kings execute thieves.
quote: இது கள் வாரை அரசர் கொல்வரென்றது.

position: உயிர்நிலை is the body, lost when the king punishes.
quote: களவினைப் பயில்வார்க்குத் தம்மின் வேறல்லாத உடம்பும் தவறும்;

position: உயிர்நிலை is release, so thieves miss liberation just as non-thieves gain heaven.
quote: பிறர் பொருளைக் கள்வார்க்கு உயிர்நிலையாகிய வீடு பெறுதல் தப்பும்;

position: It is life itself, and the gods' world becomes a world of fame.
quote: களவை நினைத்தும் பார்க்காதவர்க்கோ, புகழுலக வாழ்க்கை தவறவே தவறாது.

note: Both move the offence to the planning mind: 204 says that merely plotting ruin sets virtue plotting in return, and 282 says that merely thinking of theft is wrong. Parimelazhagar reads the standard in 282 as one for renunciants, while 204 has no such limit.

Both describe prosperity that seems to exist and then vanishes: stolen gain 'as if growing' in 283, and in 479 the life of one who doesn't live by measure, which seems to exist and is gone. Both also turn on அளவு, so here the moral and the economic meanings of 'measure' meet.
659 says that what is taken with tears goes with tears. Together they make the same bet about ill-gotten gain, but 283 stresses its illusion of growth and 659 stresses its justice.

position: Reporting what actually occurred is excluded as the definition of truth.
quote: இதனான் நிகழ்ந்தது கூறல் என்பது நீக்கப்பட்டது.

position: Truth and falsehood are classified by effect: useful non-fact is truth, and harmful or useless fact is falsehood.
quote: 'தீங்கு பயவாத நிகழ்ந்தது கூறலும், நன்மை பயக்கும் நிகழாதது கூறலும் மெய்ம்மை'

position: Without bodily strain: it spares the toil that wealth-gathering and fasting demand.
quote: மறுமைக்கு மெய் வருந்தாமல் அவனுக்கு எல்லா அறங்களையும் தானே கொடுக்கும்.

position: Without his knowing: virtue accrues to him unawares.
quote: பொய்யாமையானது அவனறியாமல் தானே எல்லா அறங்களையுங் கொடுக்குமாதலான்,

position: It brings benefits that never leave.
quote: என்றும் நீங்காத அறவழி நலன்களை அளிப்பது அந்த வாழ்வேயாகும்.

position: Truthfulness alone suffices, and it is better to skip other virtues than to attempt many and fail.
quote: அவன் பிற அறங்களைச் செய்யாமையே செய்யாமையே நன்று.

position: The opposite stress: other virtues are good only if truthfulness is unfailing, and otherwise they turn bad.
quote: பொய்யாமையைப் பொய்யாமல் செலுத்துவனாயின், பிற அறங் களைச் செய்தல் நன்றாம்; அல்லது தீதாம்,

position: The rejected lamps are worldly lights such as sun, moon and fire, which dispel outer darkness only.
quote: புறத்து இருள் கடியும் உலகத்தார் விளக்குகள் எல்லாம் விளக்கு ஆகா;

position: விளக்கு is the radiance of a good person, and what is rejected is radiance earned by other virtues.
quote: சான்றோர்க்கு எல்லாவறத்தினாலும் உண்டான ஒளியும் ஒளி யல்ல ;

note: 300 finds nothing better than truthfulness, while 323 puts not killing first and truthfulness right behind it. The Kural declares its rankings chapter by chapter, and here it comes close to correcting itself.

Almost the same phrase is applied to opposite things: பொய்யா விளக்கு is truthfulness here, and 753 calls wealth the பொய்யா விளக்கம் that cuts through darkness. The section on wealth deliberately takes over the language of the section on virtue.
297 prizes unbroken not-lying, while 292 admits falsehood under a condition. They are consistent only given 291's redefinition of truth by effect, which shows how much that definition is carrying.
225 favours giving over austerity, the commentators on 263 favour austerity over giving, and 295 now sets truth above both. The chapters rank a shifting set of virtues rather than a fixed ladder.
278 shows the bathers with impure minds, and 298 states the principle that this water only reaches the body. Read together, the chapter on hypocrisy provides the case for this general claim.

position: 'Kills' means intense suffering: the ascetic loses his austerity by cursing and is back in the misery of births.
quote: கொலைச்சொல் ஈண்டுத் துன்பமிகுதி உணர்த்தி நின்றது.

position: Anger endangers life itself.
quote: இஃது உயிர்க்கேடு வருமென்றது.

position: இனம் means fellow renunciants who teach, the raft that crosses the sea of births to release.
quote: முற்றத் துறந்து தவஞானங்களால் பெரியயராய்க் கேட்டார்க்கு உறுதி பயக்கும் மொழிகளை இனியவாகச் சொல்லுவாரை.

position: இனம் means one's friends, who bring one ashore from a sea of sorrow.
quote: தன்னைக் கரையேற விடுகின்ற நட்டோராகிய புணையைச் சுடும்.

position: இனம் means one's kin.
quote: அவரைப் பாதுகாக்கும் தோணி போன்ற சுற்றத்தையும் அழித்துவிடும்.

position: The image is about certainty: the ruin can no more miss than a hand can miss the ground.
quote: நிலத்தின்கண் அறைந்த அவன் கை அந்நிலத்தையுறுத்தல் தப்பாதவாறு போலத் தப்பாது.

position: The image is about rebound: it is the striker's own hand that hurts.
quote: நிலத்தைக் கையால் அறைந்தவனுக்கு அவன் கைதான் வலிக்கும்.

position: They equal those who have attained release, since knowledge is certain for them though they still have a mortal body.
quote: 'வீடு பெற்றாரோடு ஒப்பர்'

position: They equal those who have given up all possessions.
quote: அதனை யொழிந் தார் எல்லாப் பொருளையுந் துறந்தாரோடு ஒப்பர்,

note: Both are about the moment of having power over someone weaker. 250 offers a memory that stops you: your own fear before the strong. 301 says that only at this moment does restraint count as virtue at all.

264 credits austerity with the power to crush foes. On Parimelazhagar's reading of 305, the ascetic who uses this power in a curse loses his austerity and returns to the misery of births. The power is real, but using it destroys its source.

Both distinguish the laughter of the face from that of the heart. 786 says that friendship that smiles only on the face isn't friendship, and 304 says anger kills both, so a smile alone isn't what is at stake.
Both ask for restraint under extreme provocation. 157 goes further and grounds it in pity for the wrongdoer's coming fall, whereas 308 offers no reason, only the admission that it is hard.
The same promise, that what one wants arrives as one wants it, is made for austerity in 265 and for non-anger in 309. On this comparison, dropping anger can do the work of austerity.

position: The prize is the yogic powers such as becoming minute, so the temptation is an ascetic one.
quote: யோகமாகிய சிறப்புத் தரும் அணிமா முதலிய செல்வங்களைப்

position: The prize is ordinary wealth, refused even when it would bring no blame.
quote: இது பழி வாராத செல்வம் பெறினும் தவிர வேண்டு மென்றது.

position: The attacker has been angered by a fault of one's own.
quote: தாஞ்செய்த குற்றத்தினாலே வெகுண்டு,

position: Present suffering comes from past harm, and harming no one now protects the future.
quote: இக் காலத்து நுகர்கின்ற துன்பமெல்லாம் முற்காலத்துப் பிறர்க் குத் துன்பம் செய்தார் மாட்டே யுளவாம் ;

note: Both use ஒறுத்தல், punish. 314 says to punish wrongdoers by shaming them with kindness; 550 says that the king punishing the worst of them with death is simply weeding a crop. The word keeps its form while the ethics of person and state divide.

Both test அறிவு by conduct toward others: 203 calls not harming enemies its peak, and 315 says it comes to nothing without guarding others from pain. Understanding here is measured morally rather than by what one knows.
207 says that the enmity of deeds can't be escaped. 319 adds speed: by the same afternoon. One closes off every direction and the other closes off time.

position: The verse exists to settle a doubt that the chapter on truth raised.
quote: இரண்டு அறந்துள்ளும் யாது சிறந்தது என்று ஐயம் நிகழுமன்றே!

position: He is the highest within the class of renunciants, who differ by sect.
quote: கொலைப் பாவத்தை அஞ்சிக் கொல்லாமை ஆகிய அறத்தை மறவாதவன் உயர்ந்தவன்.

position: He may stay a householder and still be above all who renounce.
quote: கொல்லாமையைச் சிந்திப்பான் தலைமை யுடையவன்; இல் வாழ்க்கையில் நிற்பினும்,

position: It promises a full allotted span without interruption, which gives time for knowledge and release.
quote: இப் பேரறம்செய்தான் தானும் கொல்லப்படான்; படானாகவே, அடியிற்கட்டிய வாழ்நாள் இடையூறின்றி எய்தும்

position: Death doesn't come because there will be no further birth.
quote: பிறவாமை யுண்டாமாதலால் கூற்றுச் செல்லாது என்றார்.

position: It is a tribute: death itself hesitates, in awe.
quote: சாவுகூட அவர் உயிரைப் பறிக்கத் தயங்கி நிற்கும்.

position: The case is a creature that would kill you: even then, because killing increases sin. He rejects a reading about ritual expiation.
quote: 'தன்னை அது கொல்லினும் தான் அதனைக் கொல்லற்க'

position: The case is killing for medicine in mortal illness, which some people hold is no fault.
quote: உயிர்க்குக் கேடுவருங் காலத்து நோய்க்கு மருந்தாகக் கொல்லுதல் குற்ற மன்று என் பார்க்கு, இது கூறப்பட்டது.

position: The issue is Vedic sacrifice, valid for householders seeking heaven and base only for those seeking release, so injunction and prohibition don't clash.
quote: துறக்கம் எய்துவார்க்கு ஆம் ஆயினும், வீடு எய்துவார்க்கு ஆகாது

position: Killing in sacrifice is also not acceptable, as the great seek release and let ritual go.
quote: வேள்வி யின் வரும் கொலையும் ஆகாதென்றது.

position: It is any killing that would produce great benefit, and sacrifice isn't mentioned.
quote: பெரிதாக நன்மை தரக்கூடிய அளவுக்கு ஒரு கொலை பயன்படக் கூடுமெனினும்,

position: The phrase 'whose work is killing' shows that killing in sacrifice isn't killing.
quote: 'கொலை வினையர்' என்றதனான், வேள்விக் கண் கொலையன்மை அறிக.

note: 330 reports that the diseased and destitute are paying for their killings. 1062 rages that if people must beg to live, the world's maker should perish. One explains misery as deserved, and the other refuses to accept it at all.
320 says that all pain rests on those who caused pain, looking forward. 330 turns this around and reads a past killing from present suffering.

327 forbids taking life even to save one's own. 550 likens the king's execution of murderers to weeding a crop. Here the Kural's most absolute rule meets its statecraft, and it does not reconcile them.

259 explicitly mentions sacrifice but only of oblations, and sets not killing above it. 328 doesn't mention sacrifice, but the commentators find animal sacrifice there. That shows how a commentary tradition can place a controversy in the text.
972 says that birth is alike for all and distinction comes from the work done. 329 applies this to killing: base by occupation. The commentators' emphasis on 'by work' follows the same principle.

position: The crores are thoughts and schemes.
quote: கோடியளவும் அன்றி அதனினும் பலவாய நினைவுகளை நினையா நிற்பர் அறிவிலாதார்.

position: The crores are what they assume their lifespan to be.
quote: தமது வாழ்நாளைக் கோடியுமல்ல, பலவாகக்கருதுவர் உலகத்தார்,

position: குடம்பை is the egg, since a bird grows within it and never returns, and he explicitly rejects 'nest'.
quote: முன் தனியாத முட்டை தனித்துக் கிடப்ப அதனுள் இருந்த புள்ளுப் பருவம் வந்துழிப் பறந்து போன தன்மைத்து,

position: குடம்பை is the nest, and the point is that life leaves whenever it will.
quote: கூடு தனியே கிடக்கப் புள்ளுப் பறந்து போனாற்போலும்;

position: It is the egg and the chick.
quote: உடலுக்கும் உயிருக்கும் உள்ள உறவு முட்டைக்கும் பறவைக் குஞ்சுக்கும் உண்டான உறவு போன்றதுதான்.

position: Death and birth alternate naturally and quickly, as sleep and waking do.
quote: சாக்காடும் பிறப்பும் இயல்பாய்க் கடிதின் மாறிமாறி வரும்

position: It is a statement of rebirth: the life that went is born again.
quote: போன உயிர் மீண்டும் பிறக்கு மென்பதூஉம்,

position: There is no cycle: birth is the waking and death is a sleep with no waking.
quote: திரும்ப விழிக்க முடியாத மீளா உறக்கம் கொள்வதே இறப்பு.

position: No body has ever been a permanent home to it, given how life comes and goes among bodies.
quote: எஞ்ஞான்றும் இருப்பதோர் இல் இதுகாறும் அமைந்ததில்லை போலும்!

position: The home is specifically the state of release.
quote: புக்கில் என்பது முத்தி ஸ்தானம்.

position: Once it leaves the body, life has no other shelter, which comes close to the reverse.
quote: அதனைப் பிரிந்தால் வேறு புகலிடம் கிடையாது.

note: 333 says wealth is by nature unstaying; 753 calls it the unfailing lamp that drives out darkness wherever one intends. The chapter on impermanence and the chapter on acquiring wealth describe the same thing in opposite terms.
Both tell the owner of unstable wealth where to put it. 226 names the place: the hunger of the destitute. 333 explains why it must be done immediately.
Both end உணர்வார்ப் பெறின், 'if those who perceive it could be found'. Flesh as a wound, and a day as a blade: in each, the ordinary hides violence, and the verse doubts that many will see it.
36 says not to put off virtue until later, since it is a companion that doesn't die when you die. 335 supplies the concrete deadline: before the hiccup stops the tongue.
340 asks gently whether the lodger has no home of its own. 345 draws the conclusion for one who wants to leave for good: even the lodging is too much, let alone other ties.

position: Renounce in time, while young, so as to have these joys for longer.
quote: அவ் இன்பங்களை வேண்டின், அவற்றைக் காலம் பெறத் துறக்க.

position: Renounce if you want gain for your own soul.
quote: தன்னுயிர்க்கு ஆக்கம் உண்டாக வேண்டின்,

position: Renounce while everything is still there to give up.
quote: எல்லாம் இருக்கும் போதே அவற்றைத் துறந்து விடுவானே யானால்,

position: This is the world of release, beyond even the gods' reach.
quote: வானோர்க்கும் எய்தற்கு அரிய வீட்டுலகத்தை எய்தும்.

position: This is earthly fame greater than heaven-high fame.
quote: வான்புகழையும் மிஞ்சுகின்ற உலகப் புகழுக்கு உரியவனாவான்.

position: The unattached one is the Lord, and what is held is the path to release that he taught.
quote: எல்லாப் பொருளையும் பற்றி நின்றே பற்றற்ற இறைவன் ஓதிய வீட்டு நெறியை,

position: What is held is a practice: meditative absorption.
quote: பற்றற்றான் பற்றாவது தியான சமாதி.

position: The unattached one is any person so unattached, and it is him one should hold to.
quote: எதிலும் பற்றில்லாதவராக யார் இருக்கிறாரோ அவரிடம் மட்டும் பற்றுக் கொள்ள வேண்டும்.

note: 341 says each thing given up removes that thing's pain, a piecemeal gain. 344 says keeping even one thing brings it all back. Parimelazhagar accepts both, one as a gain and the other as a risk, but the practical advice differs.

343 demands that the domain of the five senses be crushed. 1101 finds all five senses' delights gathered in the beloved. The third book takes what renunciation would destroy and fulfils it in one person.
இன்மை, having nothing, is natural and right for austerity in 344. In 1041, poverty, the same word, is what nothing else can match for misery. The word changes value completely with who has chosen it.

50 places the good householder among the gods, and 346 and 348 put full renouncers beyond them and everyone else in the net. Parimelazhagar's ladder (fame and heaven for householders, release for renouncers) is how the commentary fits these together.

7 says that only those who join the feet of the incomparable one can be rid of grief. 350 repeats the structure with attachment. Parimelazhagar himself notes that the generic word is kept to match the invocation chapter.

position: The false view is to deny rebirth, the fruit of deeds, and God.
quote: அவ் விபரீத உணர்வாவது, மறுபிறப்பும், இருவினைப் பயனும், கடவுளும் இல்லை எனவும்,

position: The five-fold awareness is the mind itself, gathered into concentration, and even this falls short.
quote: ஐந்தாகிய உணர்வு: மனம்.

position: It is all that can be known by the five senses.
quote: மெய் முதலாகிய பொறிகளைந்தினானும் அறியப்படுவனவெல்லாம் அறிந்தவிடத்தும்,

position: It is having subdued the five senses.
quote: தமது ஐம்புலன்களையும் அடக்கி வெற்றி கண்டிருந்தாலும் கூட

position: One discards the world's imputed conceptions and sees what remains.
quote: பொருள் தோறும் உலகத்தார் கற்பித்துக் கொண்டு வழங்குகின்ற கற்பனைகளைக் கழித்து, நின்ற உண்மையைக் காண்பது

position: It is about not being taken in by outward looks.
quote: வெளித்தோற்றத்தைப் பார்த்து ஏமாந்து விடாமல்,

position: 'Not coming back' means no return to birth.
quote: மீண்டு இப்பிறப்பின்கண் வாராத நெறியை எய்துவர்.

position: It means no return to the household life from renunciation.
quote: மீண்டும் இல்லற வாழ்க்கையை விரும்ப மாட்டார்கள்.

position: There is no need to expect a further birth for such a person.
quote: அவனுக்கு மாறிப் பிறப்புளதாக நினைக்க வேண்டா.

position: Those who truly investigate won't believe in rebirth at all, which reverses the claim into a denial of the doctrine.
quote: உண்மையை ஆராய்ந்து உறுதியாக உணர்பவர்கள் மீண்டும் பிறப்பு உண்டு எனக் கருத மாட்டார்கள்.

position: It means the ignorance that is the first cause of birth.
quote: பிறப்பிற்கு முதற்காரணமாய அவிச்சை கெட;

position: The folly is thinking that oneself is born and dies, when one's real standing has neither.
quote: தான் பிறந்தானாக வும் செத்தானாகவும் கருதுகின்ற அறியாமையை விட்டுத்,

position: The ignorance is the very belief in a next birth.
quote: அடுத்த பிறப்பு எனக் கூறப்படும் அறியாமையைப் போக்கித்

position: The support to be known is the supreme reality on which all rests, and the supports to end are the attachments.
quote: எல்லாப் பொருட்கும் சார்பாய அச்செம்பொருளை உணர்ந்து,

position: The support is what attaches to oneself, the dependence on deeds.
quote: சார்பு - வினைச் சார்பு;

position: It simply means finding out the causes of one's troubles and letting go of them.
quote: அத்துன்பங்களுக்குக் காரணமானவற்றை உணர்ந்து

position: The Sanskrit list of five faults reduces to these three, since ego falls under ignorance and craving under desire.
quote: இவர் அவற்றுள் அகங்காரம் அவிச்சைக்கண்ணும் அவாவுதல் ஆசைக்கண்ணும் அடங்குதலான், 'மூன்று' என்றார்.

note: Their second lines are identical. 423 applies it to what we are told: whoever says it, find the truth in it. 355 applies it to what things are: whatever their appearance, find the truth in them. The same habit of mind is both critical thinking and metaphysics.

343 demands crushing the domain of the five senses. 354, on Kalaignar's reading, says that this gets you nothing without true perception. The disciplined renouncer of chapter 35 isn't the goal in itself.
