For Parimelazhagar, the schools conflict on everything in 242 and yet converge on அருள். On 353, he says that their conflict leaves doubt only experience can settle. Together they give his view of religious pluralism: agreement in ethics, and no resolution by argument in metaphysics.
356 makes learning (கற்று) the route to seeing the true thing. 373 says however much one studies, one's own understanding prevails. Chapter 38 thus undercuts the very means this one recommends.

35 defines virtue as conduct free of envy, craving, anger and harsh words. 360 lists desire, anger and confusion, whose ending ends pain. Anger and desire appear in both lists, and the shift to confusion in 360 marks the shift from conduct to knowledge.
Both describe those of மாசறு காட்சி who are free of மருள். 352 says what it does for them; 199 says what it looks like from outside: they don't utter a meaningless word even by accident.

position: Non-birth comes of itself to one who wants to want nothing.
quote: அப்பிறவாமைதான் ஒரு பொருளையும் அவாவாமையை வேண்ட அவனுக்குத் தானே உண்டாம்.

position: It is a warning: the misery that makes one wish one had never been born comes if desires aren't eliminated.
quote: விரும்புவதானால் பிறக்காமலே இருந்திருக்க வேண்டும் என்று ஒருவன் எண்ணுகிற அளவுக்கு ஏற்படுகிற துன்ப நிலை, ஆசைகளை ஒழிக்காவிடில் வரும்.

position: வாய்மை here stands for the Supreme, who has truth, and wanting it means continuous contemplation.
quote: மெய்ம்மையுடைய பரத்தை ஆகுபெயரால் 'மெய்ம்மை' என்றும் கூறினார்.

position: வாய்மை means speaking truth, and those who speak truth come to have no desire.
quote: அவ்வாசை யின்மை மெய் சொல்லுதலை விரும்ப வரும்,

position: It deceives by acting first as a friend.
quote: வஞ்சனை செய்தல் - நன்றி செய்வாரைப் போல முன்னே நின்று , பின்னே தீக்கதியுள் உய்த்தல்.

position: ஈண்டும் means 'even here', so joy comes while still in the body.
quote: அவன் வீடு பெற்ற வழியே அன்றி உடம்போடு நின்ற வழியும் இன்பம் இடையறாது.

position: ஈண்டும் means 'it swells', so joy increases without break, and Parimelazhagar notes this view.
quote: இன்ப மானது இடையறாமல் வந்து மிகும்,

note: Both solve the same problem by the same paradox: you can't leave desire by force, so desire is used against itself. 350 holds to the one without holding, and 362 wants to be without wanting.

விழுச்செல்வம் names not wanting here and learning in 400. Taken with 241 and 411, the Kural has awarded the title of true wealth to at least four things, and that suggests the phrase is a rhetorical form and not a doctrine.

298 says inner purity comes through truth. 364 gives the missing link: purity is the absence of craving, and wanting truth brings it. On Parimelazhagar's view, the meaning of truth has shifted from speech to the Supreme.

351 traces birth to confusion and 361 traces it to craving, and both claim to be the root. Parimelazhagar makes them a sequence, with ignorance first and craving following, but the verses each say it singly.
Virtue as a kind of fear: in 201 the excellent fear evil deeds, and in 366 what is to be feared is craving, which is behind those deeds. It is the same moral fear moved one step closer to its source.

320 says all pain rests on those who caused pain, and 368 says sorrow comes from craving and doesn't come to those without it. Two single-source explanations of suffering, one ethical and one psychological, sit a few chapters apart.

Just ten verses apart, this one ends the section on renunciation by promising a nature that can't be shifted, once craving goes. 380 asks what is stronger than fate, which gets there first. The Kural moves from the highest claim for human release straight to the strongest claim against human power.
அற்றார் are the destitute in 226, to be fed, and the freed in 365, to be revered. The same word for lacking marks both the most pitiable person and the most complete one.

position: Fate itself generates the effort and sloth that help make or lose wealth.
quote: முயற்சி மடிகளையும் தானே தோற்றுவிக்கும்

position: A natural condition, not fate, gives rise to enthusiasm or laziness.
quote: ஆக்கத்திற்கான இயற்கை நிலை

position: Fate alters even the understanding one is born with.
quote: இயற்கையானாகிய அறிவையும் வேறுபடுக்கும்

position: Natural conditions of ruin and growth produce ignorance and understanding.
quote: அழிவுதரும் இயற்கை நிலை, அறியாமையை உண்டாக்கும்

position: The verse concerns one fated to folly, whose fate-given foolishness overrides what study taught.
quote: தன் ஊழான் ஆகிய பேதைமை உணர்வே மேற்படும்

position: Learning may be present, but understanding that comes from fate is stronger.
quote: கல்வியுண்டாயினும் ஊழானாய்வறிவு வலியுடைத் தென்றார்

position: Natural intelligence rises above study, with no appeal to fate.
quote: அவரது இயற்கை அறிவே மேலோங்கி நிற்கும்.

position: The 'good' and 'bad' are favourable conditions such as time, place, means and action, which fate overturns.
quote: 'நல்லவை' 'தீயவை' என்பன காலமும், இடனும், கருவியும், தொழிலும் முதலாயவற்றை.

position: Good and bad actions can end in the opposite result, which is simply the natural course.
quote: நல்ல செயல்களை ஆற்ற முற்படும்போது அவை தீமையில் போய் முடிந்துவிடுவதும்

position: Possession and loss follow fate, not care or neglect.
quote: பொருள்களின் நிலையும் போக்கும் ஊழினான் ஆவதல்லது, காப்பு இகழ்ச்சிகளான் ஆகா

position: The verse is about what one has a right to, not what fate allots.
quote: தனக்கு உரிமையல்லாதவற்றை

position: The apportioner is a deity who gives each soul the fruit of its own deeds.
quote: ஓர் உயிர் செய்த வினையின் பயன் பிறிதோர் உயிரின்கண் செல்லாமல் அவ்வுயிர்க்கே வகுத்தலின்

position: What is apportioned is an ordered way of life, and wealth is hard to enjoy without following it.
quote: வகுத்து முறைப்படுத்திய வாழ்க்கை நெறியை ஒட்டி நடக்கா விட்டால்

position: They could let go of what they lack anyway, but fate's power keeps them suffering through their attitude.
quote: கருத்து வேறுபாட்டால் துன்பமுறுகின்றது ஊழின் வலியான்

position: If afflicting feelings left them, they would renounce; the obstacle is psychological.
quote: தம்மை வருத்தக்கூடிய உணர்வுகள் வந்து வருத்தாமல் நீங்கிவிடுமானால்

position: Both are one's own earlier deeds and can't be escaped, so accepting one and resisting the other is unwise.
quote: தாமே முன் செய்து கொண்டமையானும், ஊட்டாது கழியாமையானும்

position: Fate can come through the very plan meant to avert it.
quote: தான் அவ்வுபாயமேயானும் பிறிதொன்றானும் வழியாக வந்து

position: The natural state reasserts itself over artificial arrangements.
quote: இயற்கை நிலையே முதன்மையாக வந்து நிற்பதால்

note: Here effort is fate's product. In 620, effort puts fate behind you. The tension is sharper than one between effort and fate as rivals, because 371 removes effort as an independent force.
Here one's own understanding prevails over study. In 396, knowledge flows in proportion to study.
374 separates wealth and wisdom as different fates, and 400 goes further by calling learning the only true wealth. Read together, they redefine wealth.
In Parimelazhagar's reading both rest on deeds and births: 379 accepts the fruit of past deeds, and 38 stops future births.

position: துணிவு here stands for manly swiftness, acting quickly without regard to anything else.
quote: ஆண்மையாவது, ஒன்றனையும் பாராது கடிதில் செய்வது

position: துணிவு is a settled decision reached after examining the matter.
quote: ஒரு பொருளை ஆராய்ந்து துணிதலுடைமையும்

position: What is removed is wrongdoing in his realm, such as killing and theft. It is a public duty.
quote: அறனல்லவை தன் நாட்டின் கண்ணும் நிகழாமல் கடிந்து

position: What is removed is desire and anger, the king's own inner faults.
quote: அறமல்லாத காம வெகுளியைக் கடிந்து

position: சொல் means fame: the world, joined to his renown, becomes as much as he conceives.
quote: இவ்வுலகம் தன் புகழோடு மேவித் தான் கருதிய அளவிற்றாம்

position: சொல் means his command: by it the world lies in his control.
quote: தன்னேவலாலே இவ்வுலகம் தான் கண்டாற்போலும் தன் வசத்தே கிடக்கும்

position: Though a man by birth, by his deeds he is placed apart as a god for humans.
quote: பிறப்பான் மகனேயாயினும், செய்வான் மக்கட்குக் கடவுள் என்று வேறு வைக்கப்படும்

position: He is reckoned the lord of people, a political headship with no deification.
quote: மனிதர்க்கு நாயக னென்று எண்ணப்படுவான்

position: He is honoured as the people's leader.
quote: மக்களுக்குத் தலைவன் எனப் போற்றப் படுவான்.

position: The words are the rebukes of counsellors, borne for the good they will produce.
quote: இடிக்கும் துணையாயினார் சொற்களைத் தன் செவி பொறாதாகவும்.

position: The words are reports of what others have done wrong, and the king forgives those offences. He also records a view that they are a priest's words.
quote: பிறர் செய்த குற்றங்களைக் கேட்டு வைத்தும், அதனைப் பொறுக்கவல்ல குணமுடைய

note: The king must never lack அஞ்சாமை, yet 428 calls not fearing what should be feared folly. Read together, kingly fearlessness can't mean fearing nothing.
தூங்காமை is a permanent royal quality here. 672 uses the same word to divide tasks: some should be slept on and some should not. The trait becomes a judgment about each case.
467 fixes the order, deliberate and then resolve, which supports Manakkudavar's reading of துணிவு here and sits uneasily with Parimelazhagar's action without regard to anything.
The negative of the same pair. Being hard to see and harsh of look turns great wealth into what a demon has found: 386 gives the praise, 565 the horror.
The same verb, வைக்கப்படும், raises a just ruler to இறை and a rightly living householder among the gods. Both are placed there by how they live, one in public and one at home.
389 asks the king to bear bitter words; 448 says what follows if no one speaks them: he falls with no enemy needed. Parimelazhagar's gloss on 389 uses the same idea of இடிக்கும் துணை.

position: The learner stands humbled before the teacher and is thereby foremost. Those ashamed of that posture stay low for good, having lost true learning to false pride.
quote: செல்வர்முன் நல்கூர்ந்தார் நிற்குமாறு போலத் தாமும் ஆசிரியர்முன் ஏக்கற்று நின்றும் கற்றார் தலையாயினார்

position: It is the unlearned who stand yearning like the poor, and they rank beneath the learned.
quote: அதனைக் காதலித்து நிற்றலுமன்றிக் கற்றாரிடத்தாவர் கல்லாதார்

position: The verse holds where fate does not stand against it, and so it doesn't conflict with 373.
quote: இஃது ஊழ் மாறு கொள்ளாவழியாகலின்

position: ஒருமை and எழுமை are births: learning stays with the soul as deeds do, and follows it into each birth.
quote: வினைகள்போல உயிரின்கண் கிடந்து அது புக்குழிப் புகும்

position: They are generations: what is learned in one generation protects seven generations of descendants.
quote: ஒரு தலைமுறையில் பெறும் கல்வி அறிவனாது, ஏழேழு தலைமுறைக்கும் பாதுகாப்பாக அமையும்.

position: What they desire further is learning itself, because it delights the world too. Unlike wealth, its pleasure gains from being shared.
quote: கற்றறிந்தார் பின்னும் அதனையே விரும்புவர்

position: The learned are glad when others enjoy what they enjoy. The verse is about freedom from envy, a virtue that learning brings.
quote: இஃது அழுக்காறு செய்யாது இன்புறுதல் அறமாதலின், அது கல்வியானே வருமென்றது.

note: 391 demands standing by what is learned; 140 gives the failure's verdict: those who have learned much but can't act in accord with the world are unlearned and ignorant. Conduct can cancel the very category of learned.
Both turn eyes into sores, but by different tests: lack of learning here and lack of கண்ணோட்டம், kindly regard, in 575. One verse grounds sight in knowledge and the other in compassion.

In Parimelazhagar's reading, the two make one argument across chapters: learning travels with the soul through births, while caste rank ends with the body. That is why 409 can rank learning over birth.
396 makes understanding strictly proportional to study. In Parimelazhagar's reading of 416, even a small hearing gives full greatness. Reading gains by degree and listening at once.

position: The unlearned man himself longs to speak, and this is like such a woman longing for womanhood: it gets nowhere, or brings laughter.
quote: கல்வியில்லாதவன் ஒருவன் அவையின்கண் ஒன்று சொல்லுதலை அவாவுதல்

position: The fault lies with the listener who wants to hear the unlearned, and this is like being infatuated with such a woman.
quote: கல்லாதவனின் சொல்கேட்க விரும்புவது,

position: It isn't real understanding: any good result is a chance hit, like letters traced by accident.
quote: ஏரலெழுத்துப் போல்வதோர் விழுக்காடு

position: The natural intelligence may be real. The wise simply won't accept him as distinguished in learning.
quote: அவனைக் கல்வியில் சிறந்தோன் என்று அறிவுடையோர் ஒப்புக் கொள்ள மாட்டார்கள்.

position: Wealth ruins the unlearned owner, while poverty doesn't ruin the good. That is why it is more painful.
quote: திருகல்லாரைக் கெடுக்க, வறுமை நல்லாரைக் கெடாது நிற்றலான்

position: The harm falls on others: given wealth, the unlearned make other people suffer.
quote: இது செல்வமுண்டாயின், பிறரைத் துன்பமுறுவிப்பரென்றது.

position: Caste rank ends with the body while learning goes with the soul, so learning is superior. Caste rank itself is assumed.
quote: உடலோடு ஒழியும் சாதி உயர்ச்சியினும், உயிரோடு செல்லும் கல்வி உயர்ச்சி சிறப்புடைத்து

position: The honour of learning removes the distinction of high and low altogether.
quote: உயர்ந்தவர் தாழ்ந்தவர் என்ற வேறுபாட்டைப் போக்கிவிடும்.

note: 404 denies that native brightness counts without learning; 373 says a person's own understanding prevails over any amount of study. On one reading, the Kural both dismisses innate understanding and calls it unbeatable.
Both treat wealth as worse for being held by the wrong person, but 1000 faults character and 408 faults learning. 1000's spoilt milk also shows the damage to the good thing, not only to others.

409 uses high and low birth as a working scale, even to overturn it. 972 denies the scale at the root: birth is the same for all beings, and only deeds differ. The two arguments against birth rank are different in kind.
After a chapter that places the unlearned among beasts, 414 opens a door: though you haven't studied, listen. The next chapter quietly withdraws the finality of this one.

position: ஆன்றார் here are the gods who receive sacrificial offerings. The listeners are their earthly equals.
quote: நிலத்தின்கண்ணர் ஆயினும் அவியுணவினையுடைய தேவரொடு ஒப்பர்.

position: ஆன்றார் are human sages who eat little and are full of understanding, with no sacrifice or gods.
quote: குறைந்த உணவருந்தி நிறைந்த அறிவுடன் விளங்கும் ஆன்றோர்க்கு

position: Even a little brings full greatness. Like drops of rain, the listening accumulates, so don't despise the small.
quote: அக்கேள்வி மழைத் துளைபோல வந்து ஈண்டு எல்லா அறிவுகளையும் உள ஆக்கலின்

position: Greatness comes in proportion: as much as one listens, that much greatness.
quote: நல்லவற்றை எந்த அளவுக்குக் கேட்கிறோமோ அந்த அளவுக்குப் பெருமை கிடைக்கும்

note: The same formula, செல்வத்துள் செல்வம், is given to the wealth of the ear here and to the wealth of grace in 241. 400 adds learning. The Kural's chapters each crown their own wealth, which raises the question of how they rank.
Both use the leaning staff, but 414 has listening as the staff and 415 the speaker's conduct. Read together, the staff only holds if the one speaking has conduct.
978 says greatness bows while smallness vaunts. 419 gives that a source: the bowing mouth comes from listening, so 978's humility is partly a product of hearing.

position: அற்றம் is final ruin, which understanding foresees and prevents.
quote: அரசர்க்கு அறிவு என்பது இறுதி வாராமல் காக்கும் கருவியாம்

position: அற்றம் is one's own weakness, and understanding covers one's faults, while the fort handles harm from others.
quote: இது தனக்குள்ள குற்றத்தை மறைக்கு மென்றும், பிறரால் வரும் தீமை யைக் காக்குமென்றும்

position: The mind itself is driven through the senses, as a groom drives a horse. Understanding is a separate quality of the soul.
quote: குதிரையை நிலமறிந்து செலுத்தும் வாதுவன்போல வேறாக்கி மனத்தைப் புலமறிந்து செலுத்துவது அறிவு

position: The mind may go, but the body must not follow it, and the verse chiefly concerns sexual pleasure.
quote: உள்ளஞ் சென்ற விடத்தே உடம்பையுஞ் செல்லவிடாது

position: What must not open and close is friendship with the worthy. He records another view that it is about wealth and poverty.
quote: அந்நட்பின்கண் முன் மலர்தலும் பின் கூம்புதலும் இன்றி ஒரு நிலையினாவது அறிவாம்.

position: What must not open and close is one's response to joy and sorrow, which is equanimity.
quote: இன்பம் துன்பம் ஆகிய இரண்டையும் ஒரே நிலையாகக் கருதுவதே

position: It restrains a king: he must not think that because he commands the world, no one commands him.
quote: உலகத்தையெல்லாம் யான் நியமித்தலான் என்னை நியமிப்பாரில்லை,

position: உலகம் means the elevated of earlier times, so this is following the worthy, not the crowd.
quote: முற்பட்ட உயர்ந்தாரோடு பொருந்த ஒழுகுதல் அறிவு என்றார்.

position: Even suffering from past deeds does not come harshly if it is guarded against early.
quote: இது முன்னை வினையால் வருந் துன்பமும் முற்பட்டுக் காக்கின், கடிதாக வாராதென்றது.

note: Nearly the same second line. 355 tests a thing regardless of how it appears; 423 tests it regardless of who says it. Together they strip away both of the surfaces that mislead: appearance and authority.

423 sets aside the speaker when judging what is said. 415 rests the value of words on the speaker's conduct, and Parimelazhagar says those lacking it shouldn't be heard. Who says it either doesn't matter or matters most.

In the same chapter, 423 demands testing every claim for yourself and 426 says live as the world lives. The tension is softened if உலகம் means the worthy, as Manakkudavar has it, but the verse doesn't say so.

380 says fate arrives first even when one devises another way; 429 says foresight spares one from being shaken. Manakkudavar faces this directly, allowing that early guarding softens even what comes from past deeds.

374 separates being wealthy from being wise. In Parimelazhagar's gloss on 430, all wealth is made and kept by understanding, while his gloss on 374 draws the conclusion that wealth doesn't need wisdom as its cause.
Both turn on அற்றம். Understanding is the inner fort against it, and one's own fault is the enemy that brings it. So the attacker and the defence are both within.

position: செருக்கு is intoxication from wealth, and சிறுமை is excessive desire, which he calls small because it is what small people do.
quote: மதமும் வெகுளியும் காமமும் ஆகிய குற்றங்கள்

position: செருக்கு is coveting another man's wife, and சிறுமை is any behaviour of petty people.
quote: பிறர்மனை நயத்தலும், வெகுளியும், சிறியார் செய்வன செய் தொழுகுதலும்

position: What is coming is fault, supplied from the chapter's subject; even a small fault burns away great wealth.
quote: குற்றம் வரக் கடவதாகின்ற முற்காலத்திலே அதனைக் காவாத அரசன் வாழ்க்கை

position: What is coming is suffering, and failing to prepare against it is itself the fault.
quote: இது முந்துற்றுக் காவல் செய்வன செய்யாமையும் குற்ற மென்றது.

position: It can't be counted among faults because it exceeds them all: it can dominate even when every good quality is present.
quote: குற்றத் தன்மைகள் எல்லாவற்றுள்ளும் வைத்து எண்ணப்படுவது ஒன்று அன்று; மிக்கது.

position: It isn't counted because it is contemptible: useless to self and others, it is reckoned as nothing.
quote: இஃது உலோபம் தனக்கும் பிறர்க்கும் பயன்படாமையால் ஒரு பொருளாக மதிக்கப்படாதென்றது.

note: Millet and palmyra both times: 104 inflates a small favour received, and 433 a small fault committed. The same discipline of scale runs in both directions, gratitude for others and severity with oneself.
Same shape and the same காண்கிற்பின். 190 asks anyone to see their own faults as they see others', and 436 makes the order a condition for a ruler who judges.
384 requires மானம் of a king; 432 forbids மானம் that has passed beyond dignity. The same word marks a virtue and a fault, and Parimelazhagar explicitly separates them in both places.

431 praises those without desire, and 440 tells one how to enjoy desire safely. Parimelazhagar resolves this by making the fault excess in 431, but the verses themselves pull apart. Removing and hiding are different programmes.

position: These are priests and ministers: priests handle afflictions from the gods by rites, and ministers those from people by the four policies.
quote: புரோகிதரையும் அமைச்சரையும் கூறியவாறாயிற்று.

position: These are ministers. He takes the verse's general word to refer to them, leaving priests to 441.
quote: இது மந்திரிகளைக் கூட் மாறு கூறிற்று.

position: The king should examine his counsellors before taking them on, because they are his eyes.
quote: அரசன் அத்தன்மையராய அமைச்சரை ஆராய்ந்து தனக்குத் துணையாகக் கொள்க.

position: The king should be able to outplot and kill those who plot to kill him.
quote: அரசன் தன்னைச் சூழ்ச்சியாற் கொல்ல நினைப்பாரைத் தானுஞ் சூழ்ச்சியாற் கொல்லவல்லவனாதல்

position: The ruler benefits by keeping the wise around him.
quote: அறிஞர் பெருமக்களைச் சூழ வைத்துக் கொண்டிருப்பதே

note: 444 ranks support as the chief of strengths. 471 lists it as one of four to weigh before acting, alongside the task and the opponent. The superlative here gets absorbed into a calculation there.

434 calls one's own fault the only enemy that brings ruin. 448 shows the mechanism: without those who rebuke, no outside enemy is needed. Self-correction turns out to be something a person needs other people for.

position: எச்சம் is children: effects don't differ from their causes.
quote: மனம் தூயராயினார்க்கு மக்கட்பேறு நன்று ஆகும்;

position: எச்சம் is the wealth that remains after one.
quote: மனநல்லார்க்குப் பின்பு நிற்கும் காண முதலான பொருள்கள் நல்லவாம்;

position: எச்சம் is fame.
quote: மனத்தின் தூய்மையால் புகழும்,

position: Good company keeps nurturing a goodness of mind that came from earlier good deeds.
quote: அந் நல்வினை உள்வழியும் மனநலத்தை வளர்த்து வருதலின்

position: The protection is social: good company keeps the worthy from being looked down on.
quote: இனநலம் இகழ்ச்சி வாராமற் காக்குமென்றது.

position: The verse concerns joy in the next life, which the mind's goodness yields and good company secures.
quote: ஒருவற்கு மனநன்மையானே மறுமை இன்பம் உண்டாம்;

position: He doesn't mention the next life. The verse is about the support that company gives to a firm mind.
quote: அவர் சார்ந்த இனத்தின் உறுதியும் அவருக்கு வலிமையான துணையாக

note: 373 says a person's own understanding prevails over all study; 454 says understanding only seems to be one's own and lies in one's company. These are two different accounts of where knowledge comes from, within or among others, and they don't fit together easily.
34 makes a spotless mind the whole of virtue. 455 makes that purity lean on purity of company. If so, the root of virtue in 34 has a root of its own outside the person.
114 says worthiness is seen by one's எச்சம், and 456 says purity of mind produces a good one. The same disputed word closes the loop between what is inward and what is left behind.

428 says the knowing fear what should be feared. 451 names one such object, a surprising one: not a danger, but a social circle. It only makes sense given 452's claim that company changes understanding.

position: நன்று is the good stratagem, gifts and sweet words, used on rival kings, and the error is that the task fails.
quote: வேற்று வேந்தர் மாட்டு நன்றான உபாயம் செய்தற்கண்ணும் குற்றம் உண்டாம்;

position: நன்று is kindness to anyone, and misjudged kindness comes back as harm.
quote: ஒருவருடைய இயல்பைப் புரிந்து கொண்டுதான் நன்மையைக் கூடச் செய்ய வேண்டும்.

position: The issue is tactical fit: the strong shouldn't use the means of the weak, such as gifts, and the weak shouldn't use force.
quote: தாம் வலியராய் வைத்து மெலியார்க்கு உரிய கொடுத்தல் முதலிய மூன்றனைச் செய்தலும்,

position: The issue is propriety: even if a thing can be accomplished, do only what others won't despise.
quote: முடியுமாயினும், பிறராலிகழப்படாதவற்றை எண்ணிச் செய் தல் வேண்டும்;

note: Both use முதல், capital, from the merchant's world. 449 applies it to allies and 463 to risk: a king's ledger has two different kinds of principal that he can't afford to lose.
656 forbids what the worthy condemn even if one's mother is starving, the most extreme form of Manakkudavar's reading here, that being able to succeed doesn't excuse scorned means.
464 says to avoid beginning what isn't clear. 469 adds that even with the deed and intent clear, the person is another thing to know. Clarity about the act is not clarity about the recipient.

position: Resting means total commitment: fixing mind, speech and body on the task while marching.
quote: எப்பொழுதும் மன, மொழி, மெய்களை அதன் கண் வைத்துப் பகைமேல் செல்லும் அரசர்க்கு;

position: Resting means restraint: staying within the measure of what one knows one can do.
quote: அதன் பின்பு அவ்வளவிலே நின்று, ஒழுகுவராயின்,

position: The feathers are weak enemies: even the strong fail when many combine against them.
quote: 'எளியர்' என்று பலரோடு பகைகொள்வான். தான் வலியனே ஆயினும் அவர் தொக்க வழி வலியழியும்;

position: The cart is a fortress: those who trust in strong forts learn that defences fail if the enemy grows too much.
quote: இஃது அரண் மிகுதல் நன் றென்றிருப்பார்க்குப் பகைமிகின் அரண் நில்லா தென்று கூறிற்று.

note: 220 says if helpfulness brings ruin, it is worth buying even by selling oneself. 480 says helpfulness that ignores one's means quickly destroys wealth. Aram and Porul give opposite counsel on the same act, and 480 uses the same word, ஒப்புரவு.

595 says a person's height rises with their spirit, as a lotus stem with the water. 473 says many have been broken by exactly that spirit, ஊக்கம், when it wasn't measured. One counts spirit as the measure and the other demands a measure for spirit.
Prosperity that perishes while appearing to exist or grow. 283 blames fraud and 479 blames not knowing the measure, so honest wealth and stolen wealth can fail in the same deceptive way.
385 ends the royal wealth cycle in distribution. 477 sets the limit on that distribution. Parimelazhagar explicitly connects them, sending the reader back to 385 for the way of giving.

position: Actually bow to the enemy until his time comes. Your submission makes him careless, and that is why his head falls.
quote: பணியவே, அக்காலம் வந்திறும் வழி அவர் தகைவின்றி இறுவர்.

position: Bear one's own feelings of enmity patiently, and the enemy falls by himself.
quote: தங்களின் பகையுணர்வைப் பொறுமையுடன் தாங்கிக் கொள்ள வேண்டும்.

note: 376 says what isn't yours won't stay however you guard it. 482 offers timing as the rope that keeps fortune from leaving. One denies that wealth can be held by care, the other names the means of holding it.

303 says to forget anger toward anyone, because evil is born of it. 487 keeps anger alive in secret until it can be used. The Aram book treats anger as something to give up, while the Porul book treats it as something to store.
488 advises bowing to an enemy until he can be struck. 828 warns that a weapon is hidden in an enemy's folded hands. The Kural gives the technique and the defence against it, from either side.
471 says act after weighing strengths. Parimelazhagar's 485 says that even with greater strength, wait for the time. So a favourable reckoning from 471 still isn't enough.

position: முற்றும் is a verb, to besiege: don't act against an enemy until you have ground for a siege.
quote: பகைவரை முற்றுதற்கு ஆவதோர் இடம் பெற்றபின் அல்லது;

position: முற்றும் is to complete: don't begin any deed until you see where it can be finished, and don't treat it as easy.
quote: முடியுமிடங் கண்டாலல்லது, யாதொரு வினையுந் தொடங்கா தொழிக; எளிதென்றிகழாதொழிக,

position: முற்றும் is 'fully': choose a completely right place.
quote: முற்றிலும் சரியான இடத்தைத் தேர்ந்தெடுத்து அச்செயலில் இறங்க வேண்டும்.

position: துன்னியார் are the kings who have marched there and who stay close to their fort.
quote: தாம் வினை செய்தற்கு ஏற்ற இடத்தினை அறிந்து சென்ற அரசர்;

position: துன்னியார் are allies acting with one mind, so the verse is about concord among friends as well as place.
quote: வினைசெய்யும் இடமறிந்து நட்டோரானவர் மனம் பொருந்திச் செய்வாராயின்.

position: The elephant is one that strikes down spearmen. He rejects the variant வேலாழ், because a wounded elephant makes the jackal's success unremarkable.
quote: 'வேலாழ் முகத்த' என்று பாடம் ஓதுவாரும் உளர்; வேற்படை குளித்த முகத்தவாயின் அதுவும் நரி அடுதற்கு ஏதுவாய் முடிதலின், அது பாடம் அன்மை அறிக.

position: The elephant's face has spears sunk in it: he follows the variant reading.
quote: கண்ணஞ்சாத வேலழுத்தப்பட்ட முகத்தினையுடைய களிற்றைக்

note: The crow beats the owl by day and the crocodile wins in water. Time and place are two axes of the same argument: strength isn't an attribute of a creature but of a creature in a circumstance.

In Parimelazhagar's reading, 471 says to act only if your side is stronger. 493 says the weak can win by choosing the ground. If so, the calculation of 471 must already have place in it, or 471's rule is too strict.

444 calls greater people as support the chief of all strengths; 497 says no support is needed but fearlessness, if the thinking and place are right. Five chapters later, the book seems to qualify its own superlative.

A great elephant is undone in both: by a tiger's spirit in 599 and by a jackal in the mud here. One verse credits the attacker's ஊக்கம் and the other only the ground, so size loses for two quite different reasons.

position: These are four entrapment tests from Sanskrit polity, in which agents tempt the minister with staged plots, wealth, a woman and threats. Passing shows he won't change in future.
quote: உபதை நான்கின் திறத்தான் மனவியல்பு ஆராய்ந்தால் பின்பு தெளியப்படும்.

position: These are qualities to look for: firm in virtue, honest with money, not lost in pleasure and unafraid for his life.
quote: தன்னுயிருக்கு அஞ்சாதவனாகவும் இருப்பவனையே ஆய்ந்தறிந்து ஒரு பணிக்கு அமர்த்த வேண்டும்.

position: High birth is one of the qualifications in its own right, alongside the others.
quote: உயர்ந்த குடியில் பிறந்து; குற்றத்தின் நீங்கி

position: He reverses the logic: one who is faultless and ashamed of wrong is the one to be considered high-born.
quote: இருப்பவனையே உயர்குடியில் பிறந்தவன் எனத் தெளிவு கொள்ள வேண்டும்.

position: அற்றார் are those with no kin. Without them a person lacks the worldly custom that restrains him from blame.
quote: சுற்றம் இல்லாரைத் தெளிதலை ஒழிக;

position: அற்றார் are those without moral conduct.
quote: ஒழுக்கமற்றாரைத் தேறுதலைத் தவிர்க;

position: They are those without principles, not those without kin.
quote: நெறியற்றவர்களை ஒரு பணிக்குத் தேர்வு செய்வது கூடாது.

position: வழிமுறை means descendants: the suffering passes to them, as the kin fall under the enemy.
quote: அத்தெளிவு தன் வழிமுறையினும் நீங்காத துன்பத்தைக் கொடுக்கும்.

position: வழிமுறை means hereditary succession: the error is trusting an outsider as if he were of the ministerial line, and those from such lines may be trusted.
quote: பிறனை ஆராயாதே வழிமுறையென்று தெளிந்தவனுக்கு அத் தெளிவு,

note: 409 ranks the learned low-born over the unlearned high-born. 502 makes good birth the first condition for trust. The two can be squared, but the book's position on birth clearly depends on what is being asked.
349 has rebirth cut only when பற்று is gone. On Parimelazhagar's reading, 506 won't trust anyone without பற்று. The same absence is liberation in Aram and a security risk in Porul.
433 treats one's own millet-sized fault as a palm. 504 takes others on balance, by what predominates. Read together, the Kural sets a different standard for judging oneself and judging others.
972 says standing differs because of deeds, and 505 makes deeds the touchstone. Together they offer a test of worth that doesn't refer to birth, and this is at odds with 502, three verses earlier.
791 says of friendship what 510 says of ministers: examine first, because afterwards there is no way out. Both make trust something with a fixed before and after.

position: The ruler inspects the officer's conduct. The officer is the one point through which the whole world can be checked.
quote: வினை செய்வான் கோடாது ஒழிய உலகம் கோடாது;

position: The state checks on workers' condition. If those who labour don't wither, the world's prosperity doesn't wither.
quote: உழைப்போர் உள்ளம் வாடாமல் இருக்கும் வரையில் உலகின் செழிப்பும் வாடாமல் இருக்கும்.

note: 510 says doubting one you have trusted brings endless trouble. 520 says inspect him every day. Parimelazhagar sees this and calls for private inspection, but the problem of watching without doubting remains.

501 builds an elaborate test and, in Parimelazhagar's words, passing shows the person won't change. 514 says that many change anyway, through the work itself. The most careful selection can't test for what office will do.

The king creates, gathers, guards and apportions in 385; the officer enlarges, increases and watches in 512. Parimelazhagar connects them. The servant's job is a copy of the master's, without the giving.
507 condemns trusting on fondness alone. 513 puts love first among four qualities, so the fault in 507 lies in the 'alone', not in the love.

position: Each kinsman is to be regarded according to his own standing; treating all alike would make the eminent leave.
quote: எல்லாரையும் ஒரு தன்மையராக நோக்காது அரசன் தத்தம் தகுதிக்கு ஏற்ப நோக்குமாயின்

position: The verse is about singling out one person: it is the advice to appoint a crown prince.
quote: இஃது ஒருவனை இளவரசாக்க வேண்டுமென்றது.

position: All people are equal, and regard should follow ability, not rank.
quote: அனைத்து மக்களும் சமம் எனினும், அவரவர்க்குரிய ஆற்றலுக்கேற்ப அவர்களைப் பயன்படுத்திக் கொண்டால்,

position: The cause was in the king. If he removes it, they come back by themselves, as natural affection returns without being won again.
quote: அவ்வமராமைக் காரணம் தன் மாட்டு இல்லையாகத் தானே உளதாம்.

position: The cause was their pretext. They come back on realising it doesn't hold up.
quote: அந்தக் காரணம் பொருந்தாது என்று உணரும்போது மீண்டும் உறவு கொள்ள வருவார்கள்.

note: Both show wealth as a full tank. In 215 it is a public pond serving all, and in 523 it has no banks. The first image is about access, the second about containment: wealth has to be held to be shared.
212 says all wealth earned exists to serve the worthy. 524 says its fruit is being surrounded by kin. Both state the purpose of wealth, with different beneficiaries, and neither mentions the other.
521 declares that kin stay in adversity. 796 calls adversity a measuring rod for kin, which assumes some won't stay. A generalisation about kin in 53 becomes a test of them in 80.

position: What is praised is what polity texts prescribe to kings, and lapsing means hell, as with neglect of caste duty.
quote: நீதி நூலுடையார் இவை அரசர்க்கு உரியன என்று உயர்த்துக் கூறிய செயல்களைக் கடைப்பிடித்துச் செய்க;

position: What is praised is virtue, as praised by the exalted, and the verse is about not neglecting it.
quote: இஃது அறத்தின்கண் இகழாமற் செய்வது கூறிற்று.

position: They are one's duties, and neglect means no rise in life. He doesn't mention births.
quote: அப்படிச் செய்யாமல் புறக்கணிப்பவர்களுக்கு வாழ்க்கையில் உயர்வே இல்லை.

position: The memory is a corrective to mood: thinking 'we too would fall that way' stops one exulting.
quote: கெட்டாரை உள்ளவே, 'நாமும் அவ்வாறே கெடுதும்' என்று அதன்கண் மைந்துறார் என்பது கருத்து

position: It leads to a specific precaution: a king should have what he eats, wears and smears checked, because past kings died that way.
quote: இஃது உண்பவை, உடுப்பவை, பூசுபவை சோதித்துக் கொள்க என்றது.

note: 305 says anger kills the one who has it. In Parimelazhagar's argument for 531, anger at least sometimes reaches the enemy, while elated forgetting only kills oneself. The Aram book's worst self-destroyer gets demoted.
In Parimelazhagar's reasoning on 408, poverty doesn't ruin the good. 532 makes chronic poverty the very image of what destroys understanding. Either understanding survives poverty, or it doesn't.

421 builds an inner fort of understanding. 534 shows an outer fort falling to inner fear. Together they say that a fortress is finally a state of mind, which is unusual in a Porul section that counts forts as a limb of the state.

'Nothing is hard' appears with different conditions: 462 counsel, 472 knowing strength, 483 means and time, and here attention. The refrain's repetition suggests that no single one suffices, and each chapter has claimed the last word.
Same structure: what one has in mind is attained, if. 666's condition is firmness and 540's is continued remembering. They might be one quality seen from the will and from attention.

position: அந்தணர் நூல் is the Veda: beginningless itself, but it needs the sceptre in order to operate.
quote: வேதமும் அறனும் - அநாதியாயினும், செங்கோல் இல்வழி நடவா ஆகலின்,

position: They are books of the virtuous, with no reference to the Veda or to Brahmins.
quote: ஓர் அரசின் செங்கோன்மைதான் அறவோர் நூல்களுக்கும் அறவழிச் செயல்களுக்கும் அடிப்படையாக அமையும்.

position: It is a literal effect: sky and earth work together and yield abundance where rule is just.
quote: வானும் நிலனும் சேரத் தொழிற்பட்டு வளம் சுரக்கும் என்பதாம்.

position: It is a comparison: just government is like seasonal rain and a fine harvest.
quote: பெய்யும் மழையினால் வளமான விளைச்சல் கிடைப்பதற்கு ஒப்பானதாகும்.

position: The king is to punish by death those who burn, poison, rob, and those who desire another's wife. Not doing so harms the world.
quote: அரசன் கொடியவர்களைக் கொலையான் ஒறுத்துத் தக்கோரைக் காத்தல்;

position: The cruel are a narrower list: thieves, highway robbers and plunderers.
quote: கொடியாராவார் கள்வர், ஆறலைப்பார், சூறைகொள்வார்.

position: கொலை is the crime and not the penalty: the state simply punishes those who commit murder and similar cruelty.
quote: கொலை முதலிய கொடுமைகள் புரிவோரை, ஓர் அரசு தண்டனைக்குள்ளாக்குவது

note: 327 says don't take another's life even if it costs your own. 550 says the king's killing of the cruel is like weeding. The book's sharpest split between Aram and Porul: an absolute rule meets the role of king. Parimelazhagar resolves it through caste duty, which the verses don't mention.

541 makes justice not showing கண்ணோட்டம் to anyone. 578 gives the world to those able to show it without harming the work. So the king both must and must not, and 578's condition, the work unharmed, is the hinge.

528 tells a king not to look at all alike but by rank; 541 says to show no favour to anyone. Household management and the court of justice have different requirements, though they are only two chapters apart.

The chapter on rain calls it the world's nectar because it keeps the world going. 542 gives the sceptre that same place for human society, which is why the failure of one can later cause the other in 559.
30 defines அந்தணர் by compassion toward all life, and not by birth. If that is carried here, 543's அந்தணர் நூல் need not be the Veda, and this gives Kalaignar's reading a basis inside the Kural.

761 calls a fearless army the chief of a king's assets. 546 says it isn't the spear but the sceptre that gives victory. Porul itself has two answers to what wins wars, one in its justice chapter and one in its army chapter.

position: It is literal: rain in fact fails to come in season, and the next verse gives the cause.
quote: அவன் நாட்டுப் பருவமழை இன்றாம் வகை மேகம் பொழிதலைச் செய்யாது.

position: It is a practical chain: bad government lets reservoirs fall into ruin, so rain can't be stored.
quote: நீரைத் தேக்கிப் பயனளிக்கும் இடங்கள் பாழ்பட்டுப் போகுமாதலால்,

position: Those of the six duties are Brahmins. Without milk and mantras there is no sacrifice, and that is why rain fails, which completes 559.
quote: பசுக்கள் பால் குன்றியவழி அவியின்மையானும், அது கொடுத்தற்குரியார் மந்திரம் கற்பம் என்பன ஓதாமையானும், வேள்வி நடவாதாம்;

position: They are not a caste: the verse means that productive work and key occupations dwindle.
quote: ஆக்கப்பணிகள் எதுவும் நடக்காது; முக்கியமான தொழில்களும் தேய்ந்து விடும்.

note: 546 says it isn't the spear but the sceptre that wins. 552 collapses the difference: a sceptre that asks is a spear. The same pair, வேல் and கோல், marks the line between justice and its corruption.

550 has a king kill the cruel as weeds. The very next verse calls an oppressive king crueller than killers. My reading: read together, the two raise the question 550 leaves open, of who weeds the weeder, and the chapter's answer is tears, rain and time.

659 says what was taken with tears departs with tears. 555 makes the same moral arithmetic political. 659 is a personal warning about money, and here the crying of a whole people is the weapon against a throne.

1041 says nothing is more painful than poverty except poverty itself. 558 names something more painful: wealth under a tyrant. The later chapter's superlative doesn't hold in this one's political conditions.

A mirror: just rule brings rain and harvest in 545, and bent rule stops the rain in 559. Kalaignar rationalises both, a comparison in one and reservoirs in the other, because the older reading asks a modern reader to believe in moral weather.

543 makes the sceptre the origin of books and virtue, and 560 shows the effect of its absence: the books are forgotten. Parimelazhagar's chain then connects these to rain through sacrifice, which ties 11, 543 and 559 into one circle.

position: Begin as if going beyond measure, then act within measure: the penalty remains proportionate and only looks mild beside its start.
quote: அளவிறப்பச் செய்வார்போல் தொடங்கி; மெல்ல எறிக-செய்யுங்கால் அளவிறவாமல் செய்க

position: The penalty should actually be less than the offence deserves.
quote: இது குற்றத்திற்குத் தக்க தண்டத்தைக் குறையச் செய்யவேண்டு மென்றது.

position: The severity lies in admonishing to prevent wrongs, and the gentleness in the punishing itself.
quote: கண்டிக்கும்போது கடுமை காட்டித், தண்டிக்கும் போது மென்மை காட்டுகிறவர்களின்

position: The painful word is what wounded subjects say of the king, and உறை means his days: his life shrinks and his wealth goes.
quote: ஆயுளும் குறைந்து செல்வமும் கடிதின் இழக்கும்

position: உறை is where he dwells, which turns against him; even if land and residence bear it, divine force ruins him.
quote: இது நாடும் தான் உறையும் இடமும் பொறுப்பினும் தெய்வத்தினாற் கெடுவ னென்றது.

position: The harsh speech is the ruler's own, and what is lost is the regime's standing.
quote: கடுஞ்சொல் உரைக்கும் கொடுங்கோல் என்று குடி மக்களால் கருதப்படும் அரசு

position: The wealth is as if a ghost had seized it: since no one approaches, it benefits neither him nor others.
quote: அவனது செல்வம் தனக்கும் பிறர்க்கும் பயன்படாது

position: The wealth is frightening, like seeing a ghost: no one will take from it, so no army gathers.
quote: இது செல்வத்தை வாங்குவார் இன்மையின் படை சேராதென்றது.

position: He leaves deliberation to his ministers without sharing it, then rages at them when it fails, and they withdraw from him in fear.
quote: அமைச்சர்மேல் வைத்து அவரோடு தானும் எண்ணிச் செய்யாத அரசன்

position: The context is justice: he does not examine others' offences together with his council, and acts from anger.
quote: பிறர் செய்த குற்றத்தைத் தனக்கு இனமானாரோடே அமைந்து ஆராயாத அரசன்

position: The fault is a failure to consult, followed by anger and crooked conduct, and the regime falls by itself.
quote: கூட்டாளிகளிடம் கலந்து பேசாமல் சினத்திற்கு ஆளாகிக்

note: 549 clears the king: punishing crime is no blemish but his work. 567 marks where that clearance ends, since punishment past the limit becomes a file on his own strength.
386 promises praise to the king who is easy to see and not harsh of speech. 565 and 566 cost out the opposite, turning two virtues into two ways of losing wealth.
382 lists fearlessness as a king's nature. 569 suggests that it also has a material condition: without prepared defences, even a king comes to fear.
The earth in 151 patiently bears even those who dig it, the model of forbearance. In 570 that same earth finds one burden too heavy, which gives the hyperbole its force.

position: The beauty is the king's, and without it his subjects live like deer beside a tiger.
quote: கண்ணோட்டம் என்று சொல்லப்படுகின்ற சிறப்பு உடைய அழகு அரசர்மாட்டு உண்டு ஆகலான்

position: The verse is about anyone who has this quality, and they bring the world its greatness.
quote: பெரும் அழகைக் கொண்டவர்கள் இருப்பதால்தான் பெருமை அடைகிறது.

position: It means a real tree, which stands joined to earth: they walk about but are as unresponsive as trees. He rejects the plaster-puppet reading.
quote: அதனைச் சுதைமண்ணோடு கூடிய மரப்பாவை என்று உரைப்பாரும் உளர். அஃது உரையன்மை

position: It means a wooden doll made with plaster: people whose eyes have met another's and still show no regard are like the doll.
quote: சுதைமண்ணோடு கூடச் செய்த மாப்பாவையோடு ஒப்பார்

position: The task is the king's justice, which fails if he spares associates who have harmed others.
quote: முறை செய்தல் ஆகிய தன் தொழில் அழியாமல்

position: The task is the king's own interests: kindness must not cost him material loss.
quote: அரசர்க்குப் பொருட்கேடு வாராமல் கண்ணோட வேண்டுமென்று கூறிற்று.

position: பண்பினார் implies familiarity: those meant are people close to the king, and this is the top quality in kings.
quote: 'பண்பினார்' என்றதனான், அவர் பயிற்சி பெற்றாம்.

position: It extends to anyone at all who is inclined to destroy you.
quote: அழிக்க நினைத்திடும் இயல்புடையவரிடத்திலும் பொறுமை காட்டுவது

position: நாகரிகம is kindly regard, and the poison comes from associates whom one's eyes cannot refuse.
quote: நாகரிகம் என்பது கண்ணோட்டமாதல்

position: நாகரிகம is the broader possession of good qualities across virtue, wealth and pleasure.
quote: நாகரிகம் - அறம் பொருள் இன்பத்தின்கண் நற்குணங்கள் பலவும் உடைமை

note: 541 defines justice partly as not extending கண்ணோட்டம் (ஓர்ந்துகண் ணோடாது). This chapter says the world depends on it. 578 is the hinge, and Parimelazhagar cites 541 there: the same grace is the condition of the world and a corruption of justice, depending on where it falls.

578 forbids kindness that damages the work, and 580 praises kindness that swallows poison. Parimelazhagar resolves this by confining forbearance to wrongs against oneself, but the verses themselves don't state that limit.

Adjacent chapters use the same phrase, நிலக்குப் பொறை, for two different faults: the alliance of harshness with ignorance, and the mere lack of kindly regard. The second is far milder and yet receives the same verdict.
Both call failed eyes wounds. In 393 the eye is failed by lack of learning, and in 575 by lack of kindly regard. Taken together, an eye must both know and regard, and neither alone saves it.

If Manakkudavar's reading of 576 is right, both verses use the wooden doll for a person hollow inside: 1020 lacks shame and 576 lacks regard. On Parimelazhagar's reading the image is a rooted tree, and this parallel fades.

807 says those of long affection don't give it up even when ruined by friends. 580 gives the same stance its most extreme image. If Parimelazhagar is right that the poisoner is an associate, the poison verse belongs to the same ethic as the chapter on old friendship.

position: 'Everyone' is the three classes named in 584, and what is known is their good and bad words and acts.
quote: 'எல்லார்க்கும்' என்றது மூன்று திறத்தாரையும்.

position: 'Everyone' is the surrounding kings, whether enemy, ally, middle or neutral, and both their circle and his own.
quote: பகைவராகியும் நட்டாராகியும் மத்திமராகியும் உதாசீனராகியும் இருக்கின்ற அரசர்க்கும்

position: He lives as complete renunciants and vow-keepers such as pilgrims do, and this commentator records separately that others read படிவம் as costume.
quote: இதனுள் 'படிவம்' என்றதனை வேடமாக்கி, 'துறந்தார் வேடத்தாராகி' என்று உரைப்பாரும் உளர்.

position: He wears the costume of an ascetic and crosses the country's border to gather news.
quote: தவஞ் செய்வார் வேடத்தராகி, நாட்டெல்லையைக் கடந்து போய்

position: No renunciant is involved: he simply seems unconnected with the affair.
quote: நிகழ்வில் தொடர்பற்றவரைப் போலக் காட்டிக் கொண்டு

note: Both name two things as a person's eyes. 392 gives every living person numbers and letters. 581 gives a ruler spies and the treatise. Each makes sight depend on something outside the body.

In adjacent chapters a ruler's eye is first the grace that spares and then the instrument that watches everyone, kin included (584). The Kural does not reconcile the two eyes, and 578 is the nearest it comes to a rule between them.

274 condemns hiding behind ascetic practice as a hunter hides in a bush to trap birds. 586 prescribes exactly that kind of cover for the state's spy, on Manakkudavar's reading at least. The Virtue book's hypocrisy becomes the Wealth book's technique.
423 tells the individual to find the truth whoever is speaking. 589 turns the same refusal to trust a source into a state procedure, with independence and counting as its method.

position: The height gained is worldly: increase in wealth and military force.
quote: உயர்தல் - பொருள் படைகளான் மிகுதல்.

position: What is measured by the mind is energy itself, so the verse says how energy arises.
quote: மாந்தரது உள்ளத்தின் அளவினது ஊக்கம்

position: Even if fate denies kings the height, the aim stands: good people will not blame it, since their exertion did not fail.
quote: அவ்வுயர்ச்சி பால்வகையாற் கூடிற்றில்லையாயினும், அக்கருத்துத் தள்ளாமை நீர்மையுடைத்து.

position: A failed high aim is equal to having achieved it, and is beyond blame.
quote: முயன்று பெற்றதனோடு ஒக்கும்

position: This is an instruction: even if it does not succeed, do not give up the thought.
quote: அதற்காக அந்த நினைப்பை விடக்கூடாது.

position: உள்ளம் is energy: without it the chain of effort, wealth, giving and pride never starts.
quote: ஊக்கம் இல்லையாகவே முயற்சி, பொருள், கொடை செருக்கு இவை முறையே இலவாம்

position: உள்ளம் is the eagerness to give: without it one can't take pride in being a giver.
quote: அள்ளி வழங்கும் ஆர்வம் இல்லாத ஒருவர்

note: Both turn on the same word. In 594 wealth seeks out அசைவிலா energy. In 371 அசைவின்மை is itself produced by a fate of gain. The causal arrow reverses, so the question becomes whether steadfastness is one's own at all.

The elephant carries opposite morals three verses apart: under arrows it models unbreakable resolve, and before a tiger it is bulk without resolve. Parimelazhagar accepts this by locating the difference in the tiger's energy.

Both speak of the pride of giving (செருக்கு) and both root it in exertion. 613 names the vocabulary of labour and liberality that 598 only implies, so generosity is shown to have an economic foundation.

The Kural keeps naming the one true wealth: learning in 400, what is heard in 411, grace in 241, and energy here. Each dismisses ordinary wealth, but they cannot all be the sole true possession. Each is best read as a chapter's rhetorical peak.

Tree-people appear for two different lacks: kindly regard in 576 and energy in 600, and again for human quality in 997. The tree image stands for whatever a chapter takes to be essential to being human.

position: மடியா means 'as sloth': regard it for what it is, as one says to treat fire as fire. He records the other reading.
quote: நெருப்பிற் கொடியது பிறிதின்மை பற்றி, நெருப்பை நெருப்பாகவே கருதுக

position: மடியா means killing: destroy the habit of sloth.
quote: மடி செய்தலை மடித்து ஒழுகுக

position: The wealth of world-rulers comes to them unearned, but without effort to guard it, it perishes. He records another reading, that such kings become their allies.
quote: நிலம் முழுவதும் ஆண்டாரது செல்வம் தானே வந்து எய்திய இடத்தும்

position: It is the kings of the earth themselves who, however well provided, lose out if they are slothful.
quote: பூமியையுடைய வேந்தர் பல்பொருளினாலும் அமைந்த விடத் தும் மடியுடையாராயின்

position: படி means worthiness: even those who hold the affection of worthy people get nothing.
quote: தகுதியுடையவரின் அன்புக்குப் பாத்திரமானவராக இருப்பினும்

position: The one who measured is the deity who spanned all worlds with his stride, and the verse leaves him unnamed.
quote: தன் அடியளவானே எல்லா உலகையும் அளந்த இறைவன்

position: It is a tireless human king who brings every place he goes within his footstep's range.
quote: சோர்வில்லாத ஒரு மன்னன், அவன் சென்ற இடமனைத்தையும்

note: 371 says sloth (மடி) arises from a fate of loss. This chapter treats the same மடி as a thing one can depose at will. The tension is direct, and neither chapter acknowledges the other.

The same goal, raising one's family, and the same word used differently. 602 asks one to drive out மடி, and in 1023 the deity tightens its மடி (waist-cloth) and comes ahead of the one who resolves on this. That verse's தான்முந்துறும் also echoes fate's in 380.

Both invoke Vishnu's realm as the highest measure. 610 offers it to the sleepless ruler, and 605 has just listed sleep as a boat to ruin. 1103 asks whether that realm is even as sweet as sleep on a beloved's arms. The Porul and Kamam books rank sleep and sovereignty oppositely.

784 says friendship exists to rebuke when one strays, and uses the same word இடி. If Parimelazhagar is right that the scolding in 607 comes from friends, the verse shows what happens when that duty is carried out and fails.

position: தீர்ந்தார் are those who abandoned the needed work, and the world abandons them.
quote: வினையாகிய குறையைச் செய்யாது விட்டாரை உலகம் விட்டது

position: தீர்ந்தார் are those who completed it, and the world does not leave them.
quote: வினைக் குறையை முடித்தாரினின்றும் உலகம் விடப்பட்டதன்று

position: திருவினை means wealth, and specifically a king's six limbs of state.
quote: அரசர்மாட்டு உளதாய முயற்சி அவரது செல்வத்தினை வளர்க்கும்

position: It yields excellent deeds and achievements, not wealth as such.
quote: முயற்சிதான் சிறப்பான செயல்பாடுகளுக்குக் காரணமாக அமையும்.

position: The goddesses are taken as they are, dwelling respectively in sloth and in effort, with sin's blackness assigned to the first.
quote: பாவத்தின் கருமை அதன் பயனாக முகடிமேல் ஏற்றப்பட்டது.

position: The names are mere words used to point at the energetic person and the idler.
quote: சொற்கள் முறையே முயற்சியில் ஊக்கமுடையவரையும்,

position: பொறி is fate: people blame present faults, not fruits of past deeds.
quote: உலகம் பழவினை பற்றிப் பழியாது, ஈண்டைக் குற்றமுடைமை பற்றியே பழிப்பது

position: பொறி is religious merit: lacking it is no fault, and this answers those who say effort is useless without merit.
quote: யார்க்கும் புண்ணியமின்மை குற்றமாகாது

position: The idea of blame from fate is itself wrong.
quote: விதிப்பயனால் பழி ஏற்படும் என்பது தவறு

position: தெய்வம் is fate: where it withholds, one gets a wage, and where it favours, much more. So don't wait on it.
quote: முயன்ற வினை பால்வகையால் கருதிய பயனைத் தாராதாயினும்

position: தெய்வம் stands for merit: without it there's no gain, yet effort pays in proportion to strain.
quote: புண்ணியம் இன்மையால் ஆக்கம் இல்லையாயினும்

position: It refers to God and prayer: what crying out to God won't achieve, labour will.
quote: கடவுளே என்று கூவி அழைப்பதால் நடக்காத காரியம்

position: Fate can obstruct once or twice but not always, so repeated effort outlasts it.
quote: ஊழ் ஒருகாலாக இருகாலாக அல்லது விலக்கலாகாமையின், பலகால் முயல்வார் பயன் எய்துவர்

position: They actually conquer fate, turning back the bad karma that blocks the fruit.
quote: இஃது ஊழ்தன்னையும் வெல்வ ரென்றது.

note: 380 asks what could be stronger than fate, which arrives ahead of every stratagem. 620 answers that those who keep toiling see its back. Parimelazhagar narrows the gap by saying fate blocks only a few attempts, which the two verses themselves don't say.

377 limits what even hoarders of millions can enjoy to what has been apportioned. 619 guarantees effort a wage whatever divine order decides. One sets a ceiling on enjoyment and the other a floor on reward, and they may coexist only just.
The same sword in the same hand. In 614 it stands for generosity without labour and in 727 for learning without courage in an assembly. Both say an asset is void without the disposition to use it.

position: Suffering is nothing but a stance in the mind, and it vanishes when that stance is reversed.
quote: இடும்பையாவது உள்ளத்து ஒரு கோட்பாடேயன்றிப் பிறிதில்லை

position: The thought is that this is the fruit of one's deeds.
quote: நெஞ்சினாலே வினைப்பய னென்று நினைக்கக் கெடும்

position: The thought is a practical one: how to defeat the trouble.
quote: அதனை வெல்லும் வழி யாது என்பதை அறிவுடையவர்கள் நினைத்த மாத்திரத்திலேயே

position: மேல் means 'upon them', and the verse concerns bodies in all four states of birth, targets for a sword called suffering.
quote: நாற்கதியினும் உள்ள உடம்புகள் இடும்பை என்னும் வாளுக்கு இலக்கு என்று தெளிந்து

position: மேல் means 'the superior', and the context is the hardship taken on in austerity.
quote: இது மேல் நன்மையாற் றவஞ் செய்யுங்கால் வருந் துன்பத்திற்கு அழியாதா ரைக் கூறிற்று.

position: Pleasure and pain here are those arising through work and effort, and both are held in the same way.
quote: இரண்டையும் ஒரு தன்மையாகக் கோடலின், பயன்களும் இலவாயின.

position: It concerns desire: one who doesn't lose himself in sensual pleasure isn't undone by the pain it brings.
quote: இது காமத்தால் வரும் துன்பத்திற்கு அழியாதாரைக் கூறிற்று.

note: Both use the phrase வெள்ளத் தனைய, 'as much as the flood'. In 595 the flood lifts a stalk, in a figure for the rise of energy. In 622 the flood is suffering itself, dissolved by a thought. In both the mind is what settles the scale.

Both refuse the cry over lost wealth. 593 says energy is the real asset, so the loss is small. 626 says the one who never clutched has no such cry. One rests on what you still have, and the other on how you first held it.

Both begin இன்பம் விழையான், 'not desiring pleasure'. In 615 this produces a pillar for kin through labour, and in 628 it produces a person pain can't reach. The same renunciation of pleasure serves worldly work and inner calm alike, without any talk of leaving the world.

Both ask for one response to good and bad, but they give different grounds: 379 reasons from fate that it's inconsistent to accept one and grieve the other, and 629 reasons from the training of desire, without mentioning fate.

position: This verse lists four, and 'the five' are those of 631. He criticises those who split items here to reach five.
quote: மேற்சொல்லிய அங்கங்கள் ஐந்துடனே திருந்த உடையானே அமைச்சனாவான்

position: The five are named in this verse, including the guarding of the senses, and are needed before one becomes a minister.
quote: அஞ்சாமையும், குடிகாத்தலும், இந்திரியங்களைக் காத்தலும், நூல் முகத்தானறிதலும், முயற்சியும்

position: Treatise methods must fit the prevailing ways of the world, or the world will blame them.
quote: நூல் நெறியே ஆயினும் உலக நெறியோடு பொருந்தாதன செய்யற்க

position: 'The world' means the court: the character of kings and the standing of their retinue.
quote: உலகநடை அறிதலாவது அரசர் சீலமும் பரிவாரத்திலுள்ளார் நிலைமையும் அறிதல்.

position: அறிகொன்று means destroying the understanding of those who advise, even with contempt.
quote: அறிந்து சொல்லியாரது அறிவையும் அழித்து அரசன் தானும் அறியானே ஆயினும்

position: He splits the phrase differently: 'let the king know' what the minister said, and even if he knows nothing, the minister must speak.
quote: அரசன் அமைச்சன் கூறிய பொருளை யறிக

note: 373 sets one's own understanding above study, and 636 asks for both at once: native acuity with treatises. Taken together, the opposition in 373 is not the Kural's last word on learning and nature.
140 calls the learned ignorant if they can't move in step with the world; 637 turns this into an instruction for statecraft. The Virtue book's moral rule becomes a professional one.
889 says an inner enemy holds ruin even when small as a sesame fragment; 639 gives the same inner enemy a face at the king's side and a scale, seventy crore outer foes.

position: Hearers are allies who accepted him and non-hearers are hostile parties won over. He criticises all others for reading தகையவாய் as 'having worth'.
quote: நட்பாய் ஏற்றுக் கொண்டாரைப் பின் வேறுபடாமல் பிணிக்கும் குணங்களை அவாவி

position: Those are the ones who asked and the ones who did not ask.
quote: வினாவினாரைப் பிணித்துக் கொள்ளுந் தகையவாய், வினாவாதா ரும் விரும்புமாறு

position: The 'capacities' are differences of rank by birth, learning, conduct, wealth, form and age, and to speak according to them is the virtue.
quote: குடிப்பிறப்பு, கல்வி, ஒழுக்கம், செல்வம், உருவம், பருவம் என்பவற்றான் வரும் தகுதி வேறுபாடுகள்.

position: It's the way of speaking: knowing this avoids slander, empty talk and lying, so it becomes virtue.
quote: புறங்கூறாமையும் பயனில சொல்லாமையும் பொய்கூறா மையும் உளவாம்

position: It means knowing clearly the reason for saying something.
quote: காரணத்தைத் தெளிவாக அறிந்து ஒன்றைச் சொல்ல வேண்டும்.

position: தொழில் is what is being said, and the world accepts these matters readily.
quote: சொல்லப்படும் காரியங்களை நிரல்படக் கோத்து

position: தொழில் is work to do: people rush up and ask what they must do.
quote: உலகத்தார் மேவி விரைந்து சென்று செய்யுந் தொழில் யாது என்று கேட்பர்

note: 32 says nothing brings more gain than virtue, and 644 uses the same ஊங்கு formula to put apt speech above both virtue and gain. This is either high rhetoric or a real rearrangement. Parimelazhagar makes apt speech a cause of virtue to avoid the clash.

127, in the Virtue book, says guard the tongue or suffer from its errors, and the fear is personal shame. 642 makes the same demand for a public reason, since gain and ruin follow. The same discipline serves different goals.

424 defines wisdom by the same two-part structure: making your speech enter easily and finding the fine meaning in others' words. 646 assigns it to excellence in office, so wisdom and diplomacy are shown to share a form.

position: Once done in confusion, don't go on grieving: regret displays a lack of remedy and firmness and spreads one's own shame. He says all others miss the connection.
quote: பின் இருந்து அவ்விரங்கல்களைச் செய்யாதொழிதல் நன்று.

position: If one acts at all, one should not do anything like such deeds.
quote: அவைபோல்வனவுஞ் செய்யாமையே நல்லது.

position: Having done it, the good thing is not to continue it.
quote: ஒருகால் அப்படிச் செய்து விட்டாலும் அச்செயலை மீண்டும் தொடராதிருப்பதே நன்று.

position: This overrides a general dharma rule permitting wrong to feed aged parents, wife and infant, but only for ministers, who have standing and royal duties.
quote: தீயன பலவுஞ் செய்தாயினும் புறந்தருக' என்னும் அறநூற்பொது விதி

position: It applies to anyone, with no exception: not even to relieve a mother in the throes of hunger.
quote: பசியால் துடிக்கும் தனது தாயின் வேதனையைத் தணிப்பதற்காகக்கூட

position: ஏமார்த்தல் means making the king safe with such wealth. He attacks those who read it as rejoicing, since that breaks the simile's form.
quote: பிறரெல்லாம், 'ஏமாத்தல்' என்று பாடமோதி, அதற்கு மகிழ்தல் என்றும்

position: It means delight: one enjoys what one gained by deception, and both person and wealth perish.
quote: வஞ்சத்தாலே பொருள் தேடி மகிழ்ந்திருத்தல்

note: 69 gives a mother's greatest joy as hearing her son called சான்றோன், greater than at the birth. 656 uses the same two words, ஈன்றாள் and சான்றோர், and places that standing above her hunger. Read together, the son's choice could be seen as what she would have wanted, though neither verse says so.

1041 says nothing hurts like poverty. 657 chooses extreme poverty over tainted wealth. The chapter on poverty doesn't withdraw this, so the choice is made in full knowledge of what the poverty will be.
Both state a return of harm: 319 in morning and evening, 659 in the taking and the leaving. 659 restricts it to wealth and adds the positive half, that clean gains come back.

position: Avoid deeds likely to fail, and don't flag if fate spoils a deed. He rejects the variant ஓரார் as ungrammatical.
quote: பழுதுபடும் வினைகளைச் செய்யாமையும், செய்யும் வினை தெய்வத்தான் பழுதுபட்ட வழி அதற்குத் தளராமையும்

position: Reading ஓரார்: don't dwell on the suffering that action involves, and if it comes, don't weaken.
quote: வினை செய்யுங்கால் உறும் துன்பத்தை ஓரார் ஆதலும்

position: Work to remove obstacles before they come, and don't lose heart if they still do.
quote: இடையூறு வருவதற்கு முன்பே அதனை நீக்கிட முனைவது

position: கொட்க means becoming known: conceal the deed until its end, for enemies who learn of it midway will block it.
quote: செய்யப்படும் வினையை முடிவின்க புலப்படும் வகை முன்னெல்லாம் மறைத்துச் செய்வதே திட்பமாவது

position: கொட்க means turning back: go through to the end and return, for returning midway brings harm.
quote: ஒரு வினையைத் தொடங்கினால், முடிவிலே சென்று மீளல் செய் வது ஆண்மையாவது

note: 381 makes six assets (army, people, wealth, ministers, friends, fortress) the mark of a lion among kings. Parimelazhagar's 'others' in 661 are exactly army, fort and friendship, which he says don't count as firmness. The list of assets is empty without the mind that uses them.

Two versions of the same promise: obtaining what one thinks of is easy if one keeps thinking of it (540), and if one is firm (666). The first asks for attention to be sustained, and the second for action to be.

628 prevents pain by not desiring pleasure. 669 accepts pain for the sake of the pleasure that results. One asks you to stop wanting joy and the other to work for it. They may differ in scope, since 628 speaks of how one meets pain and 669 of which tasks to take up, but neither verse says so.

position: வினை here means war: where stronger, fight, since force is what is feared; otherwise use one of the other three means (conciliation, division, gifts).
quote: இயலுமிடத்தெல்லாம் போராற் செய்தல் நன்று

position: No reference to war: act when possible, and when not, keep it in mind and wait for an opening.
quote: இயலாத காலத்து அதனை நினைந்திருந்து, இயலும் இடம் பார்த்துச் செய்க

position: Plan each task so that it becomes a means to finishing the next similar one.
quote: தொடங்கிய வினையானே பிறிதும் ஓர் வினையை முடித்தற்கு உபாயம் ஆமாறு எண்ணிச் செய்க.

position: It means setting an enemy's enemies against him, so that enmity is used against enmity.
quote: தமக்கு ஒரு பகைவர் தோன்றினால் அவர்க்குப் பகையாயினாரை அவ ரோடு பகைக்குமாறு

position: ஒட்டார் are those not allied with one's enemy, i.e. the enemy's enemies, to be made friends. He allows another sense: keeping one's own foes from joining others.
quote: தன் பகைவரோடு ஒட்டாரைத் தனக்கு நட்பாக்கிக்கோடல்.

position: ஒட்டார் are simply one's enemies, to be reconciled, and this is put ahead of doing good for one's own kin.
quote: தஞ் சுற்றத்திற்கு நல்லவை செய்தலினும், பகைவரைப் பொருந்தி நட்பாகக் கொள்ளுதலை

note: Both separate thinking from having decided. 467 condemns thinking after deciding as a disgrace, and 671 condemns delay after deciding as a fault, the one seeing it as an intellectual lapse and the other a practical one.
383 asks a ruler for தூங்காமை, sleeplessness, without condition. 672 divides this: some things should indeed be slept on. Parimelazhagar makes this connection himself.

On Parimelazhagar's reading, 673 ranks force first where one is stronger. 546 says it isn't the spear that gives victory but the king's straight sceptre. The Kural's strategy and its ethics may be speaking here to different questions. Manakkudavar's reading of 673 removes this tension.
Both warn about what enmity becomes if left to grow: 879 says fell the thorn tree young, and 674 says the left-over ember flares. 879 addresses timing, and 674 completeness.
874 says the world rests in one who can turn enmity into friendship, as a mark of character. 679 turns this into a question of scheduling: it comes before duties to friends.

969 praises those who give up life at the loss of honour, like the yak with its hair. 680 describes the weak who bow and take the terms to keep their people steady. Parimelazhagar sees this: the honourable would not choose it, so the verse only reports it.

position: The love is for one's own kin, which keeps them from harm, and the birth is in a family fit for ministry.
quote: தன் சுற்றத்தார்மாட்டு அன்புடையனாதலும்

position: The love is for the king, and 'qualities kings desire' means not desiring what the king desires.
quote: வேந்தனால் விரும்பப்படும் குணமுடைமையாவது அவன் விரும்புவனவற் றைத் தான் விரும்பாமை.

position: துணைமை is having the foreign court's ministers as support, which can calm a king's anger.
quote: தமக்கு அவரமைச்சர் துணையாந்தன்மையும்

position: துணைமை is having one's own retinue, and purity is of body and mind.
quote: தூய்மையுடைமையும், சுற்றமுடைமையும்

note: Two agents of the king, both ready for death, with opposite methods: the spy says nothing whatever is done to him (586), and the envoy says everything whatever may come (690). They share an unflinching eye: compare 585's கண்ணஞ்சாது with 686's கண் அஞ்சான்.

667 says never to scorn anyone for their form. 684 makes form (உரு) one of three requirements of the envoy. Parimelazhagar's explanation is that foreign courts respect the look of a man. The Kural is apparently distinguishing what people should do from what they in fact do.

position: Say what is of great benefit and desired, even if not asked, and don't say what is profitless, even if the king asks.
quote: எஞ்ஞான்றும் பயனிலவாயவற்றைத் தானே கேட்டாலும் சொல்லாது விடுக.

position: Say what the king wants; and if an enemy king questions an envoy about the size of the army, evade: 'Don't you know?'
quote: பகையரசன் வினாவினால், நீ அறியாததொன்றோ வென்று அளவு கூறாமை.

position: The light is the king's divinity: he guards the world while asleep, and they must act as men before gods.
quote: அவர் கடவுளரும் தாம் மக்களுமாய் ஒழுகுதல்.

position: The light is simply the headship he has obtained.
quote: அவர் பெற்று நின்ற தலைமையோடே பொருந்த ஒழுக வேண்டும்

position: It is the eminence of those in positions of government.
quote: அவர்கள் அடைந்துள்ள பெருமைக் கேற்பப் பண்புடன் நடந்து கொள்ள வேண்டும்.

note: Both use கெழுதகைமை, the privilege of old intimacy. 803 asks what good long friendship is unless such liberties are accepted as if your own. 700 says to take such liberties with a king brings ruin. Friendship and power apply opposite rules to the same bond.

638 obliges the man at the king's side to tell him what is good, even if the king destroys wise counsel. 696 and 697 advise saying what is not disliked, in the way that he wants. The same courtier is told to be fearless and to be careful. Parimelazhagar narrows the gap by reading 'wanted' as also greatly beneficial.

582 makes it a king's work to know everything happening to everyone, swiftly and always. 695 tells those near him not even to listen in on his secrets. Knowledge flows one way, and the Kural presents this imbalance as prudence, not as a problem.

388 says a king who rules justly and protects is held to be a god among people: the title is earned. On Parimelazhagar's reading of 698, the divinity belongs to any king, young or kin, and the courtier mustn't ask. Other readings of ஒளி remove the conflict.

Chapter 57 tells the king not to be dreaded, and this chapter tells the courtier how to live with one who is. Both are realistic, and the Kural addresses each party without assuming the other has listened.

Almost the same phrase, துளக்கற்ற காட்சி and நடுக்கற்ற காட்சி. In 654 unshaken clarity won't do what is degrading, even in trouble. In 699 it won't presume on favour. Steadiness shows in both failure and success.

position: They read another's sign through their own inner sign; 'parts' are outer possessions such as wealth, land, elephants.
quote: உள் நிகழும் நெறி யாவர்க்கும் ஒத்தலின், பிறர் குறிப்பறிதற்குத் தம் குறிப்புக் கருவியாயிற்று.

position: They read the mind's intent through the sign in the face, and 'parts' can be limbs of the body or of the realm.
quote: முகக் குறிப்பினாலே உள்ளக்கருத்தை அறியுமவர்களை

position: They read the face, and the offer is any post in government.
quote: எந்தப் பொறுப்பைக் கொடுத்தாவது துணையாக்கிக் கொள்ள வேண்டும்.

position: It concerns a petitioner: he need only stand before those who will read his need and resolve it, since speaking shames both.
quote: அவ்வெல்லையைக் கடந்து சொல்லுமாயின் இருவர்க்குஞ் சிறுமையாமாகலின்

position: It's the reverse relation: the king, too, must read his ministers.
quote: இஃது அமாத்தியர் குறிப்பை அரசனும் அறியவேண்டுமென்றது.

position: It concerns the reader: if he has the skill, he only needs to stand in front of someone.
quote: ஒருவரின் முகத்துக்கு எதிரில் நின்றாலே போதுமானது.

note: Chapters 71 and 110 share the title குறிப்பறிதல். 709 has the eye say what kings won't, and 1100 says that when lovers' eyes agree, words are useless. A single theory of the speaking eye serves both state intelligence and love, and neither treats speech as the deeper channel.

706 and 710 say the face and eyes can't but show what is within. 585 asks the spy to stand under suspicious eyes and let nothing spill. If the face always reveals, the spy's art should be impossible, and if the spy's art is possible, this chapter overclaims.

Both end with தான்முந்துறும், 'it gets there first'. In 380, fate gets ahead of any plan. In 707, the face gets ahead of any words. 1023 uses it again of a deity. The repeated phrase pictures a force that outruns human intention.

The Kural keeps asking what eyes are for. 577 answers kindly regard, 393 learning, and 705 reading signs. Each makes the physical eye worthless by that chapter's standard, so 'real sight' is defined differently each time.

On Parimelazhagar's reading, the courtier in 698 must treat the king as a god. 702 then gives that same comparison to the man who can read minds, so the servant who can read the god is set beside him.

position: இடை is the moment: when the assembly is willing to hear.
quote: செவ்வி; கேட்டற்கண் விருப்புடைமை.

position: இடை is the fault: think about what wrong a word could bring.
quote: சொன்னால் அதற்கு வருங்குற்றத்தை ஆராய்ந்து

position: The path is the path to liberation: it is like an ascetic falling away, with loss of fruit and scorn as well.
quote: வீடு எய்தற்பொருட்டு நன்னெறிக்கண் நின்றானொருவன்

position: It is simply someone who is on a path of life and loses his standing, and is scorned.
quote: ஒரு நெறியின்கண் நின்றார் அந்நிலைமை குலைந்தாற்போல் இகழப்படும்

position: Those with the skill to examine words are the assembly: speak in such a gathering.
quote: வழுப்படாமல் சொற்களை ஆராய்தல் வல்லார் அவைக்கண் சொல்லின்

position: They are the speakers themselves: learning shows in those who choose flawless words.
quote: மாசற்ற சொற்களைத் தேர்ந்தெடுத்து உரை நிகழ்த்துவோரிடமே

note: Two poured liquids in three verses: water on a growing bed and nectar in a yard. Nectar is much more precious than water and yet the outcome is reversed. What decides the value of speech is the ground that takes it, not the substance.

Both use the phrase கோட்டி கொளல், holding forth in company. 401 faults the speaker for lacking learning, and 720 faults the hearers for lacking fitness. Together they give both ways a speech can fail.

The adjacent chapter says fearless speech in assembly is rarer than courage in battle. 715 says that the best of all good things is holding back among elders. The chapters are a pair and Parimelazhagar reconciles them with precision: only speaking first is restrained.

position: வகை is the kinds of assembly, and வல்லவை is a capable assembly. He records a reading as 'what they have mastered'.
quote: கற்றுவல்ல அவை, அல்லா அவை என்னும் அவை வகையினை அறிந்து

position: வகை is the kinds of harm that come from a slip.
quote: தப்பினால் வருங் குற்றவகையை யறிந்து

note: 780 calls a death that brings tears to one's ruler's eyes worth begging for, in the chapter on martial pride. 723 calls those who die among enemies easy to find. The Kural holds both, and each chapter's supreme value is deflated by the other.

410 makes the unlearned like beasts beside the learned. 729 places a kind of learned person below the unlearned. Learning that seemed to separate humans from animals is here worth less than nothing if the learned can't speak.
650 uses the image of a scentless flower for those who can't expound their learning. 728 and 730 give the assembly as the place of the failure, and fear as its cause, adding a diagnosis to the image.

position: விளையுள் stands for the cultivators, தக்கார் for renunciants and brahmins, and செல்வர் for merchants, so the verse lists three kinds of people.
quote: 'விளையுள்' என்பது உழவர்மேல் நின்றது.

position: விளையுள் is land itself, fields that do not fail even when rain does.
quote: தள்ளா விளையுள் - மழையில்லாத காலத்தினும் சாவிபோகாத நிலம்.

position: The wealthy who count are those who do not spend their wealth on evil.
quote: செல்வத்தைத் தீயவழியில் செலவிடாதவர்களும்

position: The burdens are refugees and herds driven from other lands by war, misrule or famine, whom this land absorbs.
quote: பாரங்கள் - மக்கள் தொகுதியும் ஆன் எருமை முதலிய விலங்குத் தொகுதியும்.

position: The burdens are the land's own, the extra exactions laid on subjects beyond the fixed tax.
quote: குடிமையாவது கடமையொழிய வருவது.

position: The two waters are ground water and surface water, and வருபுனல் is what flows down from the hill.
quote: 'கீழ் நீர், மேல் நீர்' எனப்பட்ட தன்கண் நீரும்

position: The two waters are river and sea, and வருபுனல் is rain.
quote: ஆறு, கடல் எனும் இருபுனலும்

position: வேந்து அமைவு is mutual: the people's love for the king and his grace toward them.
quote: குடிகள் அவன்மாட்டு அன்புடையராதலும், அவன்தான் இவர்மாட்டு அருளுடையனாதலும் அடங்கின.

position: The requirement falls on the king, who must himself be of good character.
quote: இது நாட்டுக்கு அரசனும் பண்புடையனாகல் வேண்டுமென்றது.

position: The point is the absence of good government.
quote: நல்ல அரசு அமையாத நாட்டில்

note: 739 says a land that makes you labour for riches is no land. 619 says bodily labour pays its wage even where the divine does not help. The ideal of the place and the ethic of the person pull in opposite directions.

545 says rain and crops gather in the just king's land. 732 doesn't mention a king, but Parimelazhagar reads the absence of calamity through the king's virtue, which turns the land's fertility into evidence about its ruler.

The same closing move in two chapters: a land with every excellence is useless without accord with its king, and a fort with every excellence is useless without people who can act. Material conditions are never allowed to be sufficient.

position: The fort is ringed by all four defences, natural and built, and the ground is a bare waste left so enemies find no foothold.
quote: நீரரண், நிலவரண், மலையரண், காட்டரண் என இயற்கையும் செயற்கையுமாய இந்நான்கு அரணும் சூழப்படுவது அரண் என்பதாம்.

position: Any one of these is enough, whether water, bare land, hill or forest.
quote: மலையாயினும், அழகிய நிழலினையுடைய காடாயினும் உடையது அரணாம்

position: The water is a deep, wide moat.
quote: ஆழமும் அகலமும் கொண்ட அகழ்

position: நீரது means of such a nature: it is built so the defenders' position is easy, with their missiles reaching out and the enemy's not reaching in.
quote: அகத்தாரது போர்நிலைக்கு எளிதாய நீர்மையையுடையதே அரணாவது.

position: நீரது means having water: there is water easy for those inside and scarce for those outside.
quote: அகத்துறைவார்க்கு நிற்றற்கு எளிதாகும் நீரை யுடைத்தாயிருப்பது அரணாவது

note: 741 allows that a ruler may fear and protect himself behind walls. 775 counts even a blink before a spear as flight. The chapter on the state and the chapter on the warrior hold different standards for fear, and both are the Kural's.

747's fort is hard to seize from outside and vulnerable to those within. 421 calls understanding an inner fort (உள்ளழிக்கலாகா அரண்) that enemies cannot destroy from within, the very weakness Parimelazhagar finds in 747.
Fort without capable actors and army without leaders end their chapters with the same negative verdict, இல்லது and இல், making human capacity the condition of every material strength.
750 says a fort fails without capable people. In 766 four virtues are the army's ஏமம, and Parimelazhagar concludes that such men need no other fort. Read together, the people are the real wall.

position: The darkness is enmity, and the lamp reaches enemy lands on its owner's behalf.
