930 asks whether a sober drunkard, seeing another drunk, doesn't recognise his own degradation. 1145 takes the same compulsion, wanting more with each intoxication, and uses it with delight. The book that condemns drink reuses its logic to describe love without condemning it.
In 1093, the water poured into love's plot is her lowered glance. In 1147 the water is her mother's harsh words. What nourishes love moves from the most private gesture to the most hostile.

position: The friend answers the man, who has promised a quick return, and aims to stop his leaving.
quote: 'பிரிந்து கடிதின் வருவல்' என்ற தலைமகற்குத் தோழி சொல்லியது.

position: The woman answers the friend, who has told her he will come back soon.
quote: இது கடித்து வருவாரென்ற தோழிக்குத் தலைமகள் ஆற்றாமையாற் கூறி யது.

position: பார்வல் is his look back in courtship, sweet because it promised union.
quote: அவர் நோக்கு மாத்திரமும் புணர்ச்சி குறித்தமையான் நமக்கு இன்ப முடைத்தாயிருக்கும்

position: It is her own watching for his arrival, a present joy set against the anxiety of being with him.
quote: நங்காதலரை வரவு பார்த்திருக்கு மது

position: The woman answers the friend, who has said love burns only where it is, like fire, and that she should therefore bear it.
quote: 'காமம் தீயே போன்று தான் நின்ற இடத்தைச் சுடுமாகலான் நீ ஆற்றல் வேண்டும்' என்ற தோழிக்குச் சொல்லியது.

position: The friend speaks, on seeing the woman's distress after the man has left.
quote: தலைமகன் பிரிந்துழித் தலைமகளாற்றாமை கண்டு தோழிகூறியது.

note: 510 warns that trusting without examination and doubting after trust both bring endless grief, for those choosing men to work with. 1153 is that same predicament without any such procedure: there is no way to test the one she has already trusted.
Both quote 'fear not' against him. In 1149 his failure removes her shame before the town. In 1154 it raises the question of fault. One promise is doing a lot of work in her argument.
Fear of parting spoils union in 1152. By 1179 it is routine: her eyes can't sleep when he is away or when he is home. Anticipation has become a permanent condition.

position: It is a rebuke to the friend, for not sending a messenger when she could have prevented the grief.
quote: தூது விடாமை நோக்கித் தோழியோடு புலந்து சொல்லியது

position: It is about the lover, who gives her the grief of parting even while they are close.
quote: நட்பாக இருக்கும்போதே பிரிவுத்துயரை நமக்குத் தரக்கூடியவர்

note: Both use water that rises as you draw it. In 396, the well is knowledge, and more study brings more. In 1161, the well is pain, and every attempt to bail it out adds more. The image of an inexhaustible resource is the same, and it is a blessing in one and a curse in the other.

The man sets shame aside to mount the palmyra horse (1132). The woman carries shame and love in perfect balance and can drop neither (1163). The book states this asymmetry directly: he can choose and she can only bear the weight.
The man's flood simply takes his raft. The same phrase, காமக் கடும்புனல், in the woman's verse has her still swimming at midnight with no shore. The image remains and the endurance lengthens.

position: தெரிந்துணரா means they looked without considering what would follow, so they should now bear what they caused.
quote: மேல் விளைவதனை ஆராய்ந்தறியாது அன்று காதலரை நோக்கி நின்ற உண்கண்கள்

position: It means the opposite: they looked after judging him good, and now they no longer recognise that goodness.
quote: முன்பு அவர் நல்லரென்று தெரிந்து உணர்ந்து நோக்கிய உண்கண் கள்

position: The friend says he hasn't really gone away. She replies: yes, someone who loved in words and not at heart is here, but what use is that if the eyes don't see him?
quote: நெஞ்சால் விழையாது வைத்துச் சொல் மாத்திரத்தால் விழைந்தவர் இவ்விடத்தே உளர்

position: It's a question, with no claim that he's near: does anyone desire what shouldn't be desired? He has gone without wishing to see them, and the eyes still can't settle.
quote: விரும்பத்தகாததனை விரும்புவாரும் உளரோ?

note: 1076 calls base men a beaten drum because they carry secrets to others. 1180 uses the same அறைபறை for her own eyes. An image of contempt for informers becomes an image of her helplessness: her body is what informs on her.

319 says harm done to others in the morning comes back to you by itself in the afternoon. Manakkudavar's gloss on 1175 uses this same moral logic, with the eyes as offenders. A serious doctrine is applied, playfully, to a woman's own eyes.

1170 wishes the eyes could travel to him as the heart does. Next, 1171 begins the attack on them. Parimelazhagar explicitly calls 1170 a preparation for this chapter, so what looks like a change of subject is a single thought.

position: நன்னிலையர் means blameless in the friend's eyes: since he must be held faultless, what does her body matter? This is bitter.
quote: முன் இப்பிரிவின் கொடுமையறியாத என்னை இதற்கு உடம்படுத்திப் பிரிந்தவர் தவறிலராகவே வேண்டுவது

position: The condition means he should suffer as she does, which is close to a curse.
quote: நம்மைக் காதலித்த வரும் நம்மைப் போலத் துன்பமுறுவராயின்

position: It means if he is well, and so it is a loving sacrifice.
quote: காதலர் நலமாக இருப்பார் என்றால்

note: 1130 insists he lives in her heart, so he has not gone anywhere. In 1184 her mind and words are full of him, but her skin has its own view. Her body undercuts what chapter 113 argues.

Both are inventories. The man in 1133 once had shame and manliness, and now has the palmyra horse, an instrument he can use. The woman in 1183 had grace and shame, and has been left sickness and pallor. Only his new possession is a tool.
In 1149 he has left her and the talk is about her; she can't be ashamed. In 1188 she states the injustice directly: the talk notices the symptom and not who caused it.

position: The esteemed one is honoured by chaste women, and கெழீஇயிலர் means she lacks good deeds, that is, she has bad karma.
quote: கெழீஇயின்மை; நல்வினையின்மை

position: The esteemed one is honoured by the world, and the word means she becomes one without being desired.
quote: விருப்பமில்லா ராவர்

position: The verse is about the partner who withdraws love, who is then thought to lack the sense of friendship.
quote: அந்தக் காதலர் நட்புணர்வு இல்லாதவராகவே கருதப்படுவார்.

position: இசை means any word at all about him, even that he isn't coming, and she hasn't got even that.
quote: 'அவர் வாரார் என்னுஞ் சொல்லாயினும் அமையும்,' என்பதுபட நின்றது.

position: The word means his fame, and words that praise him are honey to her.
quote: அவரைப் பற்றிய புகழ் உரை என் செவிக்குச் செந்தேனாகும்.

note: 11 says that the rain, sustaining the world, is to be known as ambrosia. 1192 uses the whole opening doctrine for one person's survival. The same dependence that the Kural gives to all life at its start reappears as a lover's condition.

Both use the carrying pole (கா). In 1163, love and shame hang at the ends of her life, and the pole is breaking. In 1196, love should hang on both people. The first is a struggle within one self, and the second is a fault between two.

வன்கண் is the same word in both. In 1156 he is hard because he could speak of leaving. In 1198 she calls herself hard for going on living without a word from him. The accusation has moved from him to her.

position: The man says how he has coped: love is sweet in union and in parting alike.
quote: தான் ஆற்றிய வகை கூறியவாறு.

position: The woman rejects the friend's warning that her inability to endure will bring pain.
quote: இது நீ இவ்வாறு ஆற்றாயாகின்றது துன்பம் பயக்குமென்ற தோழிக்குத் தலைமகள் மறுத்துக் கூறியது.

position: She begs the moon not to set, so that their eyes can meet on it while both look at it.
quote: மதி இருவரானும் நோக்கப்படுதலின் இருவர் கண்ணும் அதன்கண்ணே சேர்தல்.

position: She reproaches the moon for not setting: if it set she could sleep and see him in dreams.
quote: பட்டதாயின், என் கண் உறங்கும்; உறங்கினால், அவரைக் காணலாமென் பது கருத்து.

position: She asks it not to set, to give her light to seek him out with her eyes.
quote: நான் என் கண்களால் தேடிக் கண்டுபிடித்திடத் துணையாக நீ மறையாமல் இருப்பாயாக.

note: 1202 says thinking of the beloved brings no pain, and 1207 says even thinking burns. If Parimelazhagar is right that a man speaks 1202 and a woman 1207, then the chapter makes a pointed contrast between their experience of memory.
1122 is the man's oath: the bond is like body and life. 1209 quotes the same promise, வேறல்லம், as the thing killing her. In 1124 he had said her going was death to him, and now she is the one dying.

In 1119, the man tells the moon not to appear, as no one else should have her beauty. In 1210, the woman begs the moon to stay, since it's the only thing she may share with him. His moon is a rival to exclusive possession, and hers is the only link she has.
1090 says love beats liquor because sight alone is enough. 1201 says memory alone is enough. As he moves away, the comparison holds, and needs less and less of her presence.

position: The woman herself saw the dream and says this.
quote: தலைமகன் தூது வரக் கண்டாள் சொல்லியது.

position: The friend says she dreamed that messengers came, in order to comfort the woman.
quote: இது தலைமகளாற்றுதற் பொருட்டுக் காதலர் வாராநின்றாரென்று தூதர் வாக் கனாக் கண்டேனென்று தோழி சொல்லியது.

note: 81 says the whole point of keeping a home is to tend guests. 1211 applies that duty to a dream, which can be neither fed nor refused. A woman with an empty house is still measuring her situation in terms of the householder's virtue.

In Parimelazhagar's reading of 1162, sending a message shames her because it implies she's still alive. In 1212, telling him she has survived is just what she wants, provided it's in a dream. The dream permits what her waking shame forbids.

339 says death is like sleep and birth is like waking from it, as an image of impermanence. 1216 wishes waking away altogether, for the sake of staying with her lover. If the two were read together, her wish would come close to a wish not to be reborn, though nothing in the verse says this.
Both end by accusing this town of not understanding. In 1130 he dwells in her heart, while in 1220 he comes in her dreams. The defence moves on as her grounds grow thinner.

position: வேலை is a time word, the hour of ending, and he mentions but sets aside others who take it as 'you've become a spear'.
quote: மகளிர் உயிரையுண்ணும் இறுதிக்காலமாய் இருந்தாய்.

position: The word is வேல் plus ஐ: you have become a spear that eats life. He adds evening is hot, so it's not really evening.
quote: உயிரை உண்பதாகிய வொரு வேலாயிருந்தாய்

position: Also a spear that drinks life, with the blessing made explicit.
quote: உயிரைக் குடிக்கும் வேலாக இருப்பதற்காக உனக்கோர் வாழ்த்து!

note: 759 tells the reader bluntly to make wealth, for nothing cuts an enemy's pride so sharply. 1230 gives the cost of that advice from where it falls: a man whose nature has become wealth, and a woman who is dying of it. The separate books don't reconcile the claims.

In 1135 the man complains of evening's anguish, and Parimelazhagar says love flowers at evening. 1227 makes that a full image in the woman's voice. Evening afflicts both, so longing's timetable isn't gendered, though only his has the palmyra horse.

1152 is the moment when even union was spoiled by the fear of parting, and on the commentators' reading of 1225 it was morning that brought this fear. Now that the feared thing has happened, morning is innocent. Fear has its own hours.

position: He left the pain with them when he went far away, and the friend is the speaker.
quote: இவ்வாற்றாமை நம்கண்ணே நிற்பத் தாம் சேணிடைச் சென்ற காதலரை

position: He went so that their hardship would end, which gives his journey a very different motive.
quote: நமக்குத் துன்பம் ஒழிய வேண்டி, நெடு நெறிக்கண் சென்றாரை

position: The friend addresses her: your shoulders are doing what they shouldn't.
quote: இன்ப மிகுதியால் பூரித்த நின் தோள்கள்

position: The woman speaks to her friend, who has seen her shoulders waste.
quote: பிரிவிடை யாற்றாளாகிய தலைமகள் தனது தோள் வாட்ட முற்றது கண்ட தோழிக்குச் சொல்லியது.

position: The friend says these shoulders are betraying his lack of love and his false word.
quote: இவை இங்ஙனம் செயற்பாலவல்ல.

position: The woman tells her friend that her shoulders are now thinning as well as losing their beauty.
quote: தோள் அழகழிதலே யன்றி மெலி வதுஞ் செய்யாநின்றதென்று தோழிக்குத் தலைமகள் சொல்லியது.

position: He loosened his arms out of tenderness, thinking the tight embrace would hurt her.
quote: 'இவட்கு நோம்' என்று கருதி ஒரு ஞான்று யான் நெகிழ்ந்தேனாக

position: He loosened them because he was intending to leave, and she sensed this.
quote: யான் பிரிவதாக நினைத்து, அவள் முயங்கியகைகளை நீக்கினே னாக

note: In 1114, the man says the lily would bow to the ground for shame before her eyes. In 1231, the friend says her eyes are ashamed before flowers. The same flower and the same shame have changed sides, measuring what absence has done.

1108 calls sweet the embrace that even a breeze can't split, using the verb போழ. In 1239 a breeze does split it, with the same verb போழ, and the result is the first sign of her pallor. The ideal of union and its failure are one word apart.

The same incident in two voices: in 1187 she turned slightly in his arms and pallor came, and in 1238 he loosened his arms and her forehead paled. In her telling it happens to her, and in his it is what he did.

position: She has lost her outward beauty, and will now lose her inner beauty too, meaning her dignity and restraint.
quote: முன் இழந்த புறக்கவினேயன்றி நின்ற அகக்கவினும் இழப்போம்.

position: It is bodily beauty that will fade further as she wastes away.
quote: மேலும் மேனியெழில் இழந்து மெலிந்து அழிய வேண்டியுள்ளது.

note: In 1163, love and shame hang in balance on the pole of her life, and she describes the strain. In 1247 she gives an ultimatum to drop one. Nothing has changed except that she can no longer carry them, and the next chapter tells us which goes.
In 1130 she uses 'he lives within me' to refute the town's gossip. In 1249 she uses the same fact against her own heart, to stop it from leaving. The argument that once consoled her now traps her.

In 1177 she curses her eyes to weep themselves dry. In 1244 they are eating her, and she wants them gone. The eyes haven't stopped, and her conflict with them has moved from revenge to getting rid of them.

position: The context is that he has returned from courtesans; the shame she failed to feel is shame at touching a chest they have touched.
quote: நாண் - பரத்தையர் தோய்ந்த மார்பைத் தோய்தற்கு நாணுதல்.

position: It's a general statement on women and desire, and doesn't mention any courtesans.
quote: நாணென்பதொன்று அறியார் மகளிர், காமம் காரணமாக

position: புணர்ந்து here means simply coming close, or meeting; sulking fails at first encounter.
quote: புணர்தல் - ஈண்டு மிக நணுகுதல்; எதிர்ப்படுதலுமாம்.

position: The word means after union; one can't then keep up the quarrel.
quote: கூடிக் களித்தபின் ஊடல் கொண்டு அதில் உறுதியாக இருக்க முடியுமா?.

note: 966 asks what could be gained, neither fame nor heaven, by going after those who despise you. 1255 is a direct reply from inside love: people with this sickness can't know that kind of honour. The ethics chapter on honour isn't refuted, but declared unavailable.

The sneeze appears in two contrary ways: in 1203 it threatens and doesn't come, which she reads as him not thinking of her. In 1253 it comes uncontrollably, like her desire. So his love fails to arrive and hers can't be stopped.

The same phrase, மறையிறந்து மன்று படும், in both. 1138 presents it as a general truth about women's love, with Parimelazhagar seeing her own case in it. In 1254 she says it in the first person, having once thought herself an exception.
Both tell the same story in the first person: she went to sulk, and her heart went to join him. Whichever is read first, the second confirms that this is a repeating pattern, and that she knows it.

position: 'Today' is the day of her death and மேல் is the next birth: remembering him at the moment of death is how she can reach him in the next life.
quote: இவ்வெல்லைக்கண் நினைந்தால் மறுமைக்கண் அவரை எய்தி அன்புறலாம்;

position: The verse is about this life: if she forgets, her body will fail, and the address means 'you who have no pain'.
quote: தம்மழகினை நீக்கி வளை முதலான அணிகலங்களையும் கழலவிடும்

position: The heart puts out branches, swelling and rising as a tree does, with sorrow gone.
quote: என் நெஞ்சு வருத்தமொழிந்து மேன்மேற் பணைத்தெழாநின்றது.

position: The heart climbs a tree to look for him, because from the top one can see someone coming from afar.
quote: என்னெஞ்சம் மரத்தின் மேலேறிப் பாராநின்றது

position: The man, stuck on campaign, says to himself that he wants to join his wife; மனை here stands for the wife.
quote: வேந்தற்கு உற்றுழிப் பிரிந்த தலைமகன் வினை முடிவு நீட்டித் துழித் தலைமகளை நினைந்து தன்னுள்ளே சொல்லியது.

position: The woman speaks: let the king win, and I will prepare a feast at home, with மனை meaning the kitchen.
quote: நம் காதலர்க்கு விருந்து செய்வே மாக

position: The man speaks: if the leader wins, he will feast with his wife.
quote: என் மனைவியுடன் எனக்கு மாலைப்பொழுதில் இன்ப விருந்துதான்.

position: The man fears that she may die before he gets back, and it can't be her voice, since then it would be a lament and not impatience.
quote: இது தலைமகள் கூற்றாயவழி இரங்கலாவதல்லது விதுப்பாகாமை அறிக.

position: The woman answers the friend who says that he will come: what use, if my own heart has already broken?
quote: இது வருவா ரென்ற தோழிக்குத் தலைமகள் கூறியது.

note: 1151 tells him to bring promises of quick return to those who will still be alive. 1270, in Parimelazhagar's reading, has the man finally arriving at that thought himself, from the other end of the journey and perhaps too late. The warning was given at the start of the separation, and he feels it only at the end.

591 says ஊக்கம், inner resolve, is the only true possession. In 1263, the woman names a very similar quality in உள்ளம் as his companion in leaving her. The virtue the Book of Wealth values most is what she has been left for.

If Parimelazhagar's speaker is correct, evening is a coming feast for the man in 1268, and for the woman in 1224 it comes like a killer to the execution ground. They are thinking about the same hour, far apart, and with opposite expectations.

1267 is a plan: sulk, embrace or both. 1259 records how such a plan works out: she goes to sulk, and her heart gives way. The planner in 1267 hasn't learned anything from the experience, or she has and enjoys planning anyway.

position: It's an intent that he can't himself identify, and he asks her friend to find out what it is.
quote: மடந்தையது அணியகத்துக் கிடந்து புறத்துப் புலனாகின்றதொரு குறிப்பு உண்டு.

position: It's a hidden sorrow, which shows though she conceals it.
quote: இவள் மறைக்கவும் தோற்றுகின்றதொரு துன்பம் உண்டு

position: The man tells the friend that she has hidden from him out of a false fear, and the cure is for the friend to explain that he isn't leaving.
quote: என்கண் இல்லாத தொன்றனை உட்கொண்டு அது காரணமாக என்னை மறைத்துப் போன குறிப்பு

position: The friend tells the man, in courtship, that the woman's slipping away coyly means that his plea will succeed.
quote: எதிர்ப்பட்ட தலைமகற்கு நின்குறை முடியும்; நீ இவ்விடைச் செல்லென்று தோழி கூறியது.

position: He hasn't physically left: 'left yesterday' means he made up his mind then, shown by yesterday's tenderness.
quote: 'நெருநற்றுச் செய்த தலையளியாற் பிரிவு துணியப்பட்டது' என்பாள், 'நெருநற்றுச் சென்றார்' என்றும்

position: He has actually left, and she was grieving before he went.
quote: இஃது அவர் பிரிவதன் முன்னும் பிரிவரென் றேங்கி, இன்புற்றில் மென்று தலைமகள் கூறியது.

position: The man answers: he praises her decision to go with him, as a way of telling her friend he won't be leaving at all.
quote: தன் பிரிவின்மைக் குறிப்பினை அறிவுறுப்பான், அவள் பெண்மையினைப் பிறர்மேலிட்டு வியந்து கூறியவாறு.

position: The friend speaks to the man, having seen the woman's response to news of his leaving.
quote: இது பிரிவுணர்த்திய தலைமகள் குறிப்புக்கண்டு தலைமகற்குத் தோழி சொல்லியது.

note: In Parimelazhagar's reading, 1120 is the man refusing to elope because her feet can't bear even swan's down. In 1279 she looks at those same feet, her way of saying she will walk. The compliment had been an excuse, and her glance answers it.

706 says the face shows what is in the heart, as crystal shows what is next to it, in the chapter on reading signs in court. 1273 uses crystal the same way, with a thread inside it. Courtier and lover both depend on the transparency of the surface.
In 1152 the fear of parting spoils union, and Parimelazhagar cites a poem where unusual fussing is the warning sign. 1276 makes that the very argument: too much tenderness is proof of a departure.
Both have bangles announcing the departure of the lord of the shore. In 1157 they announce it to others, and in 1277 they tell her, before she herself knows. The sign has moved inward.

position: The friend tells the man that she has seen the woman's eagerness, and uses 'us' for them both.
quote: தலைமகள் புணர்ச்சி? விதுப்பு அறிந்த தோழி, தலைமகற்குச் சொல்லியது.

position: The woman speaks to the man herself, having let go of the wish to sulk.
quote: இது புலவிக்குறிப்பு நீங்கின தலை மகள் தலைமகற்குச் சொல்லியது

position: The man speaks during a sulk that won't yield to his pleading, in order to end it.
quote: உணர்ப்புவயின் வாரா ஊடற்கண் தலைமகன் சொல்லியது.

position: The woman, seeing that he desires union, tells her own heart that this isn't the moment to sulk.
quote: இப்பொழுது ஊடுவையாயின், இக்காமஞ் செவ்விதப்பு மென்று புணர்ச்சி வேட்கையால் தலைமகள் நெஞ்சோடு கூறியது.

note: 104 says that those who know value a favour the size of a millet seed as if it were a palmyra. 1282 uses the same pair for love and sulking. The scale of ethical gratitude is used for measuring love's excess, and this time the small thing is to be removed altogether.

Both state that he doesn't truly cherish her (பேணாது) and that the eyes can't rest without seeing him (காணாது அமை-). In 1178 this is a complaint on her eyes' folly, and in 1283 it's her reason for not quarrelling. The same fact has moved from grief to an explanation.

In 1127 she won't line her eyes because he's within them and would be hidden. In 1285 the stick is what the eye can't see. In the absence, kohl was an obstacle. In his presence, he himself is like the stick, too close to be seen.

90 says that a guest wilts at a cold look as an anicham flower wilts when smelled. 1289 makes love softer still than a flower. In both, what is finest about a relationship fails at a slight change in the other person's face.

1259 tells it in her voice: I went to sulk, my heart gave way. 1290 tells it in his: she sulked with her eyes and came faster than I did. Each tells the other's defeat as a private pleasure, though for her it's defeat, and for him it's a fond memory.

position: உயிர்க்காதல் means the heart loves its own life: it won't die, and so it plans reconciliation.
quote: உயிர்க்காதல் நெஞ்சு - உயிர்மேல் காதலையுடைய என் நெஞ்சு

position: It's a heart whose love is as dear as life, and it thinks on his greatness.
quote: அவருடைய பெருமையைப் பற்றியே என்னுயிர்க் காதல் நெஞ்சம்

position: The man speaks, in a sulk that won't yield, whose heart still wants her.
quote: உணர்ப்புவயின் வாரா ஊடற்கண் தலைமகன் சொல்லியது.

position: The woman replies to the friend who asks who would help.
quote: இது தலைமகள் துணையாவார் யாரென்ற தோழிக்குக் கூறியது.

note: 796 says ruin has one benefit: it's a measuring rod for friends. 1293 applies this proverb to one's own heart, which she treats as a friend who proves false. The inner dialogue has absorbed a whole social ethic of friendship.

In 1244 her eyes eat her alive with longing, and in 1296 her heart does. The same verb is used for what are, in effect, her own organs, and these chapters keep treating her as a person being consumed by her parts.
1247 demands that the heart give up either love or shame. 1297 tells us what happened: shame got forgotten. The chapter between them, on breaking restraint, is how.

ஏதிலர், the 'stranger', has been her word for him in the town's mouth, in 1129 and 1130. In 1300 the same word is used for a stranger, and now the one who isn't one's own is one's own heart. By the end, the outsider is inside.

position: She means courtesans: go back to them, she tells the man returning from them, since they'll suffer without you. It's sarcasm.
quote: நும்மைப் பெறாது புலந்தூடியிருக்கின்ற பரத்தையரைப் போய்ப் புலவி நீக்கிப் புல்லீராயின், அவராற்றார்

position: It's a general truth about lovers: leaving a sulking partner unreconciled is cruel.
quote: ஊடல் கொண்டவரின் ஊடல் நீக்கித் தழுவாமல் விடுதல்

position: She again means the other women, and she adds that she has no right to sulk, since she has their sons to look at; so go to them.
quote: நும்மோடு ஊடிய பரத்தையரை ஊடலுணர்த்திக் கூடாதொழிதல்

position: It's about any partner who stays aloof from a sulking lover.
quote: ஊடல்புரிந்து பிணங்கியிருப்பவரிடம் அன்பு செலுத்திடாமல் விலகியே இருப்பின்

position: The man, reconciled, reflects to himself that even faultless men find this sulking lovely.
quote: தலைமகளைப் புலவி நீக்கிக் கூடிய தலைமகன் தன்னுள்ளே சொல்லியது.

position: The friend tells the woman that sulking suits courtesans, and that she shouldn't sulk at those not worth it.
quote: இது பரத்தையரோடு புலந்து கூறிய தலைமகட்குத் தோழி கூறியது.

position: The man praises both kinds of quarrel after making up.
quote: இவ்விரண்டும் வேண்டும் என்று வியந்து கூறியவாறு.

position: The woman speaks, saying that there is some good in the sulking that is then healed.
quote: இஃது உணர்தற்கு நல்லது உளதென்று தலைமகள் கூறியது.

position: The man is himself sulking, because she won't yield to his pleading.
quote: இவள் நம் காதலியல்லள்; அன்மையின், இந்நோவு அறியாள்

position: The friend tells the man this when she has come inside, knowing about his sulking.
quote: அதனை யறிந்து அகம்புக்க தோழி அவனுக்குச் சொல்லியது.

note: உப்பு is the word in both. In 1302 the salt is the sulk, measured carefully. In 1328 the salt is the sweetness of the union that follows, as Parimelazhagar glosses it. The cook's image runs through both chapters, with the same word for the seasoning and the taste.

1191 calls requited love the stoneless fruit, the ideal of enjoyment with nothing in the way. 1306 says love without quarrels is fruit gone bad or not yet ripe. So the obstacle that 1191 wishes away, 1306 says is what makes the fruit ripe.

366 warns the renunciant to fear craving (அவா), because it deceives. In 1310, the sulking man names the same craving as what drives his heart to her. He uses the moral vocabulary correctly, with no intention of following it.

position: பெண்ணியலார் means courtesans, who, lacking other virtues, have only the nature of women. They look at him as his procession passes.
quote: பரத்தையர்க்குள்ளது பெண் இயற்கை மாத்திரமே என்னுங் கருத்தால், 'பெண் இயலார்' என்றாள்.

position: It simply means all women, who think of his chest as common property.
quote: நின் மார்பைப் பெண்மை யுடையா ரெல்லாரும் தமக்குப் பொதுவாக நினைத்துக்

note: The same folk belief at two points in the story. In 1203 she longs for a sneeze as proof he's thinking of her. In 1317 he sneezes in front of her, and the same belief proves someone else is thinking of him. A sign that means what one fears can't be falsified.

In 1125, the man is clever at the friend's expense: I would remember her if I forgot. 1316 shows the woman turning this logic on him: you say you remembered, so you forgot. His own wit has become the trap.

On Parimelazhagar's reading of 1262, she keeps him in mind at death so as to reach him in the next birth. In 1315, 'this birth' is what makes her cry. Rebirth, for the renunciant a fate to escape, is in this book something lovers want to share.

In 1113, he went over her body part by part, comparing it to shoots, pearls and spears, and she was pleased to be praised. In 1320 she treats that very habit of comparing part by part as evidence that he has others in mind. The praise of chapter 112 is the root of the suspicion.

position: It is jealousy: his love is so delightful that others surely enjoy it too, and she can't stand the thought.
quote: யான் எய்தற் பாலதாய இத்தலையளி ஒழிந்தாரும் எய்துவர் எனக்கருதி, அது பொறாமையான் ஊடல்நிகழா நின்றது

position: He reverses the direction: the quarrel, between faultless lovers, builds up their love.
quote: அவர்களின் அன்பை மிகுதியாக வளர்க்கக் கூடியது.

position: Water takes on the character of the ground it's in, so men take on the nature of the women they touch, which is the reason for her sulking. It's a surprisingly suspicious reading of a famous image.
quote: நீர் தான் நின்ற நிலத்தியல்பிற்றாமாறு போலக் காதலரும் தாம் கூடிய மகளிரியல்பினராகலான்

note: 1103 asks whether the Lotus-eyed one's world is sweeter than sleeping on the arms of one's beloved. 1323 repeats the challenge to heaven with a stranger choice: it's the quarrel that outdoes heaven now. Between these two verses, love has come to value its own frictions most.

In 1088, a warrior laments his strength being broken by her forehead, and takes it as defeat. In 1327, the man has worked out that losing is the way to win. The book's military imagery, which begins with injury, ends in a pleasantly ruined scoreboard.

In 1169, the woman in separation says the long nights are crueller than the cruel man himself. In 1329, the man in reunion prays for night to lengthen. The same long night is torment or wish, depending on whether the other person is there.

942 says the body needs no medicine if one eats only after the last meal has digested. 1326 takes the same physician's advice and makes it a rule of love: the pause between meals is what keeps appetite and health.

Both say soft words are the weapon that breaks her defences. In 1258 she says it with bitterness and calls him a thief, and in 1324 she says it with something like eagerness. The weapon hasn't changed, and what she wants from it has.
